BitField.description: Prescale Counter\nNote: Update prescale counter value will reset internal 8-bit prescale counter and 24-bit up counter value.
BitField.name: PSC

BitField.description:
Inter-Timer Trigger Mode Enable Bit
Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.
BitField.name: INTRGEN

BitField.description: Periodic Mode Behavior Selection Enable Bit\nIf updated CMPDAT value CNT, CNT will be reset to default value.
BitField.name: PERIOSEL

BitField.description: Toggle-output Pin Select
BitField.name: TGPINSEL

BitField.description: Capture Source Selection
BitField.name: CAPSRC

BitField.description: Wake-up Function Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, while timer interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]) is 1 and INTEN (TIMERx_CTL[29]) is enabled, the timer interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to CPU.
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for event counting function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.
BitField.name: EXTCNTEN

BitField.description: Timer Active Status Bit (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the 24-bit up counter status.\nNote: This bit may active when CNT 0 transition to CNT 1.
BitField.name: ACTSTS

BitField.description: Timer Counting Mode Select
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Timer Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, when the timer time-out interrupt flag TIF is set to 1, the timer interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Timer Counting Enable Bit\nNote 3: Set enable/disable this bit needs 2 * TMR_CLK period to become active, user can read ACTSTS (TIMERx_CTL[25]) to check enable/disable command is completed or not.
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS [0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will be set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.\nWhen user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, the transition on the capture source matches the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will be set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.
BitField.name: CAPDAT

BitField.description: Timer External Count Phase
BitField.name: CNTPHASE

BitField.description: Timer Capture Function Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the capture input function.
BitField.name: CAPEN

BitField.description: Capture Function Selection\nNote 1: When CAPFUNCS is 0 and CAPIF becomes 1, the current 24-bit timer counter value (CNT value) will be saved to CAPDAT field.\nNote 2: When CAPFUNCS is 1 and CAPIF becomes 1, the current 24-bit timer counter value (CNT value) will be saved to CAPDAT field then CNT value will be reset to 0 immediately.
BitField.name: CAPFUNCS

BitField.description: Timer Capture Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CAPIEN

BitField.description: Timer Capture De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx_EXT pin or ACMP output is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CAPDBEN

BitField.description: Timer External Counter Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CNTDBEN

BitField.description: Internal Capture Source Select\nNote: These bits only available when CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) is 1.
BitField.name: ICAPSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Edge Detect\nWhen the first capture event is generated, the CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be reset to 0 and first CAPDAT (TIMERx_CAP[23:0]) should be to 0.\nNote: Set CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) and ICAPSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPEDGE

BitField.description: Event Counter Source Selection to Trigger Event Counter Function
BitField.name: ECNTSSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Source Divider Scale\nThese bits indicate the divide scale for capture source divider. \nNote: Sets CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) and ICAPSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPDIVSC

BitField.description:
Timer Capture Interrupt Flag
This bit indicates the timer capture interrupt flag status.
Note 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
Note 2: When CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, the transition on the capture source matches the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, this bit will be set to 1 by hardware. 
Note 3: There is a new incoming capture event detected before CPU clearing the CAPIF status. If the above condition occurred, the timer will keep register TIMERx_CAP unchanged and drop the new capture value.
BitField.name: CAPIF

BitField.description: Capture Latch Interrupt Flag Overrun Status (Read Only)\nNote: This bit will be cleared automatically when user clears corresponding CAPIF.
BitField.name: CAPIFOV

BitField.description: Trigger Source Select Bit\nThis bit is used to select internal trigger source is form timer time-out interrupt signal or capture interrupt signal.
BitField.name: TRGSSEL

BitField.description: Trigger EPWM and BPWM Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be as EPWM and BPWM counter clock source.
BitField.name: TRGPWM

BitField.description: Trigger EADC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered EADC conversion.
BitField.name: TRGEADC

BitField.description: Trigger DAC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, timer time-out interrupt or capture interrupt can be triggered DAC conversion.
BitField.name: TRGDAC

BitField.description: Trigger PDMA Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered PDMA transfer.
BitField.name: TRGPDMA

BitField.description: Function Selection\nNote: When the timer is used as PWM, the clock source of time controller will be forced to PCLKx automatically.
BitField.name: FUNCSEL

Register.description: Timer0 Capture Input Noise Filter Register
Register.name: TIMER0_CAPNF

BitField.description: Capture Noise Filter Enable
BitField.name: CAPNFEN

BitField.description: Capture Edge Detector Noise Filter Clock Selection
BitField.name: CAPNFSEL

BitField.description: Capture Edge Detector Noise Filter Count\nThese bits control the capture filter counter to count from 0 to CAPNFCNT.
BitField.name: CAPNFCNT

BitField.description: PWM Counter Enable Bit
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: PWM Counter Behavior Type
BitField.name: CNTTYPE

BitField.description: PWM Counter Mode
BitField.name: CNTMODE

BitField.description: Center Re-load\nIn up-down count type, PERIOD will load to PBUF when current PWM period is completed always and CMP will load to CMPBUF at the center point of current period.
BitField.name: CTRLD

BitField.description: Immediately Load Enable Bit\nNote: If IMMLDEN is enabled, CTRLD will be invalid.
BitField.name: IMMLDEN

BitField.description: PWM Output Mode\nThis bit controls the output mode of corresponding PWM channel.
BitField.name: OUTMODE

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Counter Halt (Write Protect)\nIf debug mode counter halt is enabled, PWM counter will keep current value until exit ICE debug mode. \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DBGHALT

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nPWM output pin will keep output no matter ICE debug mode acknowledged or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DBGNACK

Register.description: Timer0 PWM Counter Clock Source Register
Register.name: TIMER0_PWMCLKSRC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Source Select\nThe PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMRx_CLK or internal timer time-out or capture event.\nNote: If TIMER0 PWM function is enabled, the PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMR0_CLK, TIMER1 interrupt events, TIMER2 interrupt events, or TIMER3 interrupt events.
BitField.name: CLKSRC

Register.description: Timer0 PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale Register
Register.name: TIMER0_PWMCLKPSC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale \nThe active clock of PWM counter is decided by counter clock prescale and divided by (CLKPSC + 1). If CLKPSC is 0, then there is no scaling in PWM counter clock source.
BitField.name: CLKPSC

BitField.description: Clear PWM Counter Control Bit\nIt is automatically cleared by hardware.
BitField.name: CNTCLR

BitField.description:
PWM Period Register
In up count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
In down count type: PWM counter counts from PERIOD to 0, and restarts from PERIOD.
In up-down count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, then decrements to 0 and repeats again.
In up and down count type:
Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description: PWM Comparator Register\nPWM CMP is used to compare with PWM CNT to generate PWM output waveform, interrupt events and trigger EADC to start conversion.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description: Dead-time Counter (Write Protect)\nThe dead-time can be calculated from the following two formulas: \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTCNT

BitField.description: Enable Dead-time Insertion for PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nDead-time insertion function is only active when PWM complementary mode is enabled. If dead- time insertion is inactive, the outputs of PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 are complementary without any delay.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTEN

BitField.description: Dead-time Clock Select (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTCKSEL

BitField.description: PWM Counter Value Register (Read Only)\nUser can monitor CNT to know the current counter value in 16-bit period counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: PWM Counter Direction Indicator Flag (Read Only)
BitField.name: DIRF

BitField.description: PWM Level-detect Brake Interrupt Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKLIEN

BitField.description: PWM Zero Point Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches 0.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: ZIF

BitField.description:
PWM Period Point Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches PERIOD.
Note 1: In up-down count type, PIF flag means the center point flag of current PWM period.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Up Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in up count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP is equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPUIF flag in up count type and up-down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPUIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP is equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPDIF flag in down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPDIF

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKEIF0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKEIF1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKLIF0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKLIF1

BitField.description: Edge -detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF0 1 to clear BRKEIF0 flag and PWMx_CH0 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF1 1 to clear BRKEIF1 flag and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS1

BitField.description: PWM Counter Event Source Select to Trigger Conversion
BitField.name: TRGSEL

BitField.description: PWM Counter Event Trigger EADC Conversion Enable Bit\nNote: Set TRGSEL (TIMERx_PWMTRGCTL[2:0]) to select PWM trigger conversion source.
BitField.name: TRGEADC

BitField.description: PWM Synchronous Mode Enable Select
BitField.name: SYNCMODE

BitField.description: PWM Synchronous Counter Start/Clear Source Select\nNote 1: If TIMER0/1/2/3 PWM counter synchronous source are from TIMER0, TIMER0_PWMSCTL[8], TIMER1_PWMSCTL[8], TIMER2_PWMSCTL[8] and TIMER3_PWMSCTL[8] should be 0.\nNote 2: If TIMER0/1/ PWM counter synchronous source are from TIMER0, TIMER0_PWMSCTL[8] and TIMER1_PWMSCTL[8] should be set 0, and TIMER2/3/ PWM counter synchronous source are from TIMER2, TIMER2_PWMSCTL[8] and TIMER3_PWMSCTL[8] should be set 1.
BitField.name: SYNCSRC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Synchronous Trigger Enable Bit (Write Only)\nPMW counter synchronous function is used to make selected PWM channels (including TIMER0/1/2/3 PWM, TIMER0/1 PWM and TIMER2/3 PWM) start counting or clear counter at the same time according to TIMERx_PWMSCTL setting.\nNote: This bit is only available in TIMER0 and TIMER2.
BitField.name: STRGEN

BitField.description: PWM Counter Equal to 0xFFFF Flag\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CNTMAXF

BitField.description: Trigger EADC Start Conversion Flag\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: EADCTRGF

BitField.description: PWM Period Buffer Register (Read Only)\nUsed as PERIOD active register.
BitField.name: PBUF

BitField.description: PWM Comparator Buffer Register (Read Only)\nUsed as CMP active register.
BitField.name: CMPBUF

Register.description: Timer0 PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Register
Register.name: TIMER0_PWMIFA

BitField.description: PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Counter\nThis field sets the count number which defines (IFACNT+1) times of specify PWM interrupt occurs to set IFAIF bit to request the PWM accumulator interrupt. \nPWM accumulator flag (IFAIF) will be set in every (IFACNT+1) times during the the PWM counter operation.
BitField.name: IFACNT

BitField.description: PWM Accumulator Stop Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: STPMOD

BitField.description: PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Source Select
BitField.name: IFASEL

BitField.description: PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Enable Bit
BitField.name: IFAEN

Register.name: TIMER0_PWMAINTSTS

BitField.description:
PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when the accumulator value reaches (IFACNT+1)
Note 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
Note 2: If APDMAEN (TIMERx_PWMAPDMACTL[0]) is set, this bit will be auto clear after PDMA transfer done.
BitField.name: IFAIF

Register.description: Timer0 PWM Accumulator Interrupt Enable Register
Register.name: TIMER0_PWMAINTEN

BitField.description: PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: IFAIEN

Register.name: TIMER0_PWMAPDMACTL

BitField.name: APDMAEN

Register.name: TIMER0_PWMEXTETCTL

BitField.name: CNTACTS

BitField.description: External Trigger Pin Selection
BitField.name: EXTTRGS

Register.name: TIMER1_CAPNF

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMCLKSRC

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMCLKPSC

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMMSKEN

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMMSK

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMBNF

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMFAILBRK

Register.description: Timer1 PWM Pin Output Polar Control Register
Register.name: TIMER1_PWMPOLCTL

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMPOEN

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMSWBRK

Register.description: Timer1 PWM Interrupt Flag Accumulator Register
Register.name: TIMER1_PWMIFA

Register.description: Timer1 PWM Accumulator Interrupt Flag Register
Register.name: TIMER1_PWMAINTSTS

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMAINTEN

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMAPDMACTL

Register.name: TIMER1_PWMEXTETCTL

BitField.description: Prescale Counter\nNote: Update prescale counter value will reset internal 8-bit prescale counter and 24-bit up counter value.
BitField.name: PSC

BitField.description:
Inter-Timer Trigger Mode Enable Bit
Setting this bit will enable the inter-timer trigger capture function.
The Timer0/2 will be in event counter mode and counting with external clock source or event.Also, Timer1/3 will be in trigger-counting mode of capture function.
Note: For Timer1/3, this bit is ignored and the read back value is always 0.
BitField.name: INTRGEN

BitField.description: Periodic Mode Behavior Selection Enable Bit\nIf updated CMPDAT value CNT, CNT will be reset to default value.
BitField.name: PERIOSEL

BitField.description: Toggle-output Pin Select
BitField.name: TGPINSEL

BitField.description: Capture Source Selection
BitField.name: CAPSRC

BitField.description: Wake-up Function Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, while timer interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]) is 1 and INTEN (TIMERx_CTL[29]) is enabled, the timer interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to CPU.
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Event Counter Mode Enable Bit \nThis bit is for event counting function enabled. \nNote: When timer is used as an event counter, this bit should be set to 1 and select PCLK as timer clock source.
BitField.name: EXTCNTEN

BitField.description: Timer Active Status Bit (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the 24-bit up counter status.\nNote: This bit may active when CNT 0 transition to CNT 1.
BitField.name: ACTSTS

BitField.description: Timer Counting Mode Select
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description: Timer Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, when the timer time-out interrupt flag TIF is set to 1, the timer interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Timer Counting Enable Bit\nNote 3: Set enable/disable this bit needs 2 * TMR_CLK period to become active, user can read ACTSTS (TIMERx_CTL[25]) to check enable/disable command is completed or not.
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nTIMER counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
Timer Comparator Value
CMPDAT is a 24-bit compared value register. When the internal 24-bit up counter value is equal to CMPDAT value, the TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS [0] Timer Interrupt Flag) will be set to 1.
Note 1: Never write 0x0 or 0x1 in CMPDAT field, or the core will run into unknown state.
Note 2: When timer is operating at continuous counting mode, the 24-bit up counter will keep counting continuously even if user writes a new value into CMPDAT field. But if timer is operating at other modes, the 24-bit up counter will restart counting from 0 and using newest CMPDAT value to be the timer compared value while user writes a new value into CMPDAT field.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: Timer Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of timer while 24-bit timer up counter CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) value reaches CMPDAT (TIMERx_CMP[23:0]) value.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TIF

BitField.description: Timer Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of timer.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: TWKF

BitField.description:
Timer Data Register
Read operation.
Read this register to get CNT value. For example:
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 0, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit counter value.
If EXTCNTEN (TIMERx_CTL[24]) is 1, user can read CNT value for getting current 24-bit event input counter value.
Write operation.
Writing any value to this register will reset current CNT value to 0 and reload internal 8-bit prescale counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: Timer Data Register Reset Active (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates if the counter reset operation active.\nWhen user writes this CNT register, timer starts to reset its internal 24-bit timer up-counter to 0 and reload 8-bit pre-scale counter. At the same time, timer set this flag to 1 to indicate the counter reset operation is in progress. Once the counter reset operation done, timer clear this bit to 0 automatically.
BitField.name: RSTACT

BitField.description: Timer Capture Data Register\nWhen CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, the transition on the capture source matches the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, CAPIF (TIMERx_EINTSTS[0]) will be set to 1 and the current timer counter value CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be auto-loaded into this CAPDAT field.
BitField.name: CAPDAT

BitField.description: Timer External Count Phase
BitField.name: CNTPHASE

BitField.description: Timer Capture Function Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the capture input function.
BitField.name: CAPEN

BitField.description: Capture Function Selection\nNote 1: When CAPFUNCS is 0 and CAPIF becomes 1, the current 24-bit timer counter value (CNT value) will be saved to CAPDAT field.\nNote 2: When CAPFUNCS is 1 and CAPIF becomes 1, the current 24-bit timer counter value (CNT value) will be saved to CAPDAT field then CNT value will be reset to 0 immediately.
BitField.name: CAPFUNCS

BitField.description: Timer Capture Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CAPIEN

BitField.description: Timer Capture De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx_EXT pin or ACMP output is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CAPDBEN

BitField.description: Timer External Counter Pin De-bounce Enable Bit\nNote: If this bit is enabled, the edge detection of TMx pin is detected with de-bounce circuit.
BitField.name: CNTDBEN

BitField.description: Internal Capture Source Select\nNote: These bits only available when CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) is 1.
BitField.name: ICAPSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Edge Detect\nWhen the first capture event is generated, the CNT (TIMERx_CNT[23:0]) will be reset to 0 and first CAPDAT (TIMERx_CAP[23:0]) should be to 0.\nNote: Set CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) and ICAPSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPEDGE

BitField.description: Event Counter Source Selection to Trigger Event Counter Function
BitField.name: ECNTSSEL

BitField.description: Timer Capture Source Divider Scale\nThese bits indicate the divide scale for capture source divider. \nNote: Sets CAPSRC (TIMERx_CTL[22]) and ICAPSEL (TIMERx_EXTCTL[10:8]) to select capture source.
BitField.name: CAPDIVSC

BitField.description:
Timer Capture Interrupt Flag
This bit indicates the timer capture interrupt flag status.
Note 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
Note 2: When CAPEN (TIMERx_EXTCTL[3]) bit is set, the transition on the capture source matches the CAPEDGE (TIMERx_EXTCTL[14:12]) setting, this bit will be set to 1 by hardware. 
Note 3: There is a new incoming capture event detected before CPU clearing the CAPIF status. If the above condition occurred, the timer will keep register TIMERx_CAP unchanged and drop the new capture value.
BitField.name: CAPIF

BitField.description: Capture Latch Interrupt Flag Overrun Status (Read Only)\nNote: This bit will be cleared automatically when user clears corresponding CAPIF.
BitField.name: CAPIFOV

BitField.description: Trigger Source Select Bit\nThis bit is used to select internal trigger source is form timer time-out interrupt signal or capture interrupt signal.
BitField.name: TRGSSEL

BitField.description: Trigger EPWM and BPWM Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be as EPWM and BPWM counter clock source.
BitField.name: TRGPWM

BitField.description: Trigger EADC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered EADC conversion.
BitField.name: TRGEADC

BitField.description: Trigger DAC Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, timer time-out interrupt or capture interrupt can be triggered DAC conversion.
BitField.name: TRGDAC

BitField.description: Trigger PDMA Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to 1, each timer time-out event or capture event can be triggered PDMA transfer.
BitField.name: TRGPDMA

BitField.description: Function Selection\nNote: When the timer is used as PWM, the clock source of time controller will be forced to PCLKx automatically.
BitField.name: FUNCSEL

Register.description: Timer2 Capture Input Noise Filter Register
Register.name: TIMER2_CAPNF

BitField.description: Capture Noise Filter Enable
BitField.name: CAPNFEN

BitField.description: Capture Edge Detector Noise Filter Clock Selection
BitField.name: CAPNFSEL

BitField.description: Capture Edge Detector Noise Filter Count\nThese bits control the capture filter counter to count from 0 to CAPNFCNT.
BitField.name: CAPNFCNT

BitField.description: PWM Counter Enable Bit
BitField.name: CNTEN

BitField.description: PWM Counter Behavior Type
BitField.name: CNTTYPE

BitField.description: PWM Counter Mode
BitField.name: CNTMODE

BitField.description: Center Re-load\nIn up-down count type, PERIOD will load to PBUF when current PWM period is completed always and CMP will load to CMPBUF at the center point of current period.
BitField.name: CTRLD

BitField.description: Immediately Load Enable Bit\nNote: If IMMLDEN is enabled, CTRLD will be invalid.
BitField.name: IMMLDEN

BitField.description: PWM Output Mode\nThis bit controls the output mode of corresponding PWM channel.
BitField.name: OUTMODE

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Counter Halt (Write Protect)\nIf debug mode counter halt is enabled, PWM counter will keep current value until exit ICE debug mode. \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DBGHALT

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nPWM output pin will keep output no matter ICE debug mode acknowledged or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DBGNACK

Register.description: Timer2 PWM Counter Clock Source Register
Register.name: TIMER2_PWMCLKSRC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Source Select\nThe PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMRx_CLK or internal timer time-out or capture event.\nNote: If TIMER0 PWM function is enabled, the PWM counter clock source can be selected from TMR0_CLK, TIMER1 interrupt events, TIMER2 interrupt events, or TIMER3 interrupt events.
BitField.name: CLKSRC

Register.description: Timer2 PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale Register
Register.name: TIMER2_PWMCLKPSC

BitField.description: PWM Counter Clock Pre-scale \nThe active clock of PWM counter is decided by counter clock prescale and divided by (CLKPSC + 1). If CLKPSC is 0, then there is no scaling in PWM counter clock source.
BitField.name: CLKPSC

BitField.description: Clear PWM Counter Control Bit\nIt is automatically cleared by hardware.
BitField.name: CNTCLR

BitField.description:
PWM Period Register
In up count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, and restarts from 0.
In down count type: PWM counter counts from PERIOD to 0, and restarts from PERIOD.
In up-down count type: PWM counter counts from 0 to PERIOD, then decrements to 0 and repeats again.
In up and down count type:
Note: User should take care DIRF (TIMERx_PWMCNT[16]) bit in up/down/up-down count type to monitor current counter direction in each count type.
BitField.name: PERIOD

BitField.description: PWM Comparator Register\nPWM CMP is used to compare with PWM CNT to generate PWM output waveform, interrupt events and trigger EADC to start conversion.
BitField.name: CMP

BitField.description: Dead-time Counter (Write Protect)\nThe dead-time can be calculated from the following two formulas: \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTCNT

BitField.description: Enable Dead-time Insertion for PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nDead-time insertion function is only active when PWM complementary mode is enabled. If dead- time insertion is inactive, the outputs of PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 are complementary without any delay.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTEN

BitField.description: Dead-time Clock Select (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: DTCKSEL

BitField.description: PWM Counter Value Register (Read Only)\nUser can monitor CNT to know the current counter value in 16-bit period counter.
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: PWM Counter Direction Indicator Flag (Read Only)
BitField.name: DIRF

Register.description: Timer2 PWM Output Mask Enable Register
Register.name: TIMER2_PWMMSKEN

BitField.description: PWMx_CH0 Output Mask Enable Bit\nThe PWMx_CH0 output signal will be masked when this bit is enabled. The PWMx_CH0 will output MSKDAT0 (TIMERx_PWMMSK[0]) data.
BitField.name: MSKEN0

BitField.description: PWMx_CH1 Output Mask Enable Bit\nThe PWMx_CH1 output signal will be masked when this bit is enabled. The PWMx_CH1 will output MSKDAT1 (TIMERx_PWMMSK[1]) data.
BitField.name: MSKEN1

BitField.description: Enable Internal ACMP1_O Digital Output As Edge-detect Brake Source (Write Protect)\nNote 1: Only internal ACMP1_O signal from low to high will be detected as brake event.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: Enable PWMx_BRAKEy Pin As Edge-detect Brake Source (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: Enable Internal ACMP1_O Digital Output As Level-detect Brake Source (Write Protect)\nNote 1: Only internal ACMP1_O signal from low to high will be detected as brake event.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: Enable PWMx_BRAKEy Pin As Level-detect Brake Source (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: Enable System Fail As Level-detect Brake Source (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: PWM Brake Action Select for PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: PWM Brake Action Select for PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKAODD

Register.description: Timer2 PWM Pin Output Polar Control Register

BitField.description: PWMx_CH0 Output Pin Polar Control Bit\nThe bit is used to control polarity state of PWMx_CH0 output pin.

BitField.description: PWMx_CH1 Output Pin Polar Control Bit\nThe bit is used to control polarity state of PWMx_CH1 output pin.

Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

Refer toSYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: PWM Zero Point Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches 0.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: ZIF

BitField.description:
PWM Period Point Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter reaches PERIOD.
Note 1: In up-down count type, PIF flag means the center point flag of current PWM period.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Up Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in up count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP is equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPUIF flag in up count type and up-down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPUIF

BitField.description:
PWM Compare Down Count Interrupt Flag
This bit is set by hardware when TIMERx_PWM counter in down count direction and reaches CMP.
Note 1: If CMP is equal to PERIOD, there is no CMPDIF flag in down count type.
Note 2: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPDIF

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKEIF0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Interrupt Flag PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKEIF1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH0 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKLIF0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Interrupt Flag on PWMx_CH1 (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.\nNote 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: BRKLIF1

BitField.description: Edge -detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF0 1 to clear BRKEIF0 flag and PWMx_CH0 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS0

BitField.description: Edge-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: User can set BRKEIF1 1 to clear BRKEIF1 flag and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKESTS1

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH0 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.
BitField.name: BRKLSTS0

BitField.description: Level-detect Brake Status of PWMx_CH1 (Read Only)\nNote: If TIMERx_PWM level-detect brake source has released, both PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 will release brake state when current PWM period finished and resume PWMx_CH0 and PWMx_CH1 output waveform start from next full PWM period.

BitField.name: FDCKS5

BitField.description:
Transition Mask Counter
The fault detect result will be masked before counter count from 0 to TRMSKCNT.

FDCKS is set to 0: 
Mask time is EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT+2)
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Mask time EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT+2)

Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSCn[11:0]) is 0:
BitField.name: TRMSKCNT

BitField.description: Fault Detect Mask Enable Bit
BitField.name: FDMSKEN

BitField.description:
Deglitch Sampling Cycle
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSCn[11:0]) is 0:
BitField.name: DGSMPCYC

BitField.description:
Transition Mask Counter
The fault detect result will be masked before counter count from 0 to TRMSKCNT.

FDCKS is set to 0: 
Mask time is EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT+2)
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Mask time EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) * (TRMSKCNT+2)

Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSCn[11:0]) is 0:
BitField.name: TRMSKCNT

BitField.description: Fault Detect Mask Enable Bit
BitField.name: FDMSKEN

BitField.description:
Deglitch Sampling Cycle
FDCKS is set to 0: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
FDCKS is set to 1: 
Sampling detect signal each EPWMx_CLK * CLKPSC * (2^FDCKSEL) period and detect DGSMPCYC+1 times
Note:
CLKPSC (EPWM_CLKPSCn[11:0]) is 0:
BitField.name: DGSMPCYC

BitField.description: Rising Dead-time Counter (Write Protect)\nThe Rising dead-time can be calculated from the following formula: \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: RDTCNT

BitField.description: Falling Dead-time Counter (Write Protect)\nThe dead-time can be calculated from the following formula: \nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description: Enable Rising Dead-time Insertion for EPWM Pair (Write Protect)\nRising Dead-time insertion is only active when this pair of complementary EPWM is enabled. If rising dead- time insertion is inactive, the outputs of pin pair are complementary without any delay.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: RDTEN0

BitField.description: Enable Rising Dead-time Insertion for EPWM Pair (Write Protect)\nRising Dead-time insertion is only active when this pair of complementary EPWM is enabled. BitField.description: Enable Falling Dead-time Insertion for EPWM Pair (Write Protect)\nFalling Dead-time insertion is only active when this pair of complementary EPWM is enabled. BitField.description: Enhanced Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter \nA 32-bit up/down counter. When an effective phase pulse is detected, this counter is increased by one if the bit DIRF (EQEI_STATUS[8]) is one or decreased by one if the bit DIRF(EQEI_STATUS[8]) is 0. This register performs an integrator which count value is proportional to the encoder position. The pulse counter may be initialized to a predetermined value by one of three events occurs:
BitField.name: CNT

BitField.description: Enhanced Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter Hold\nWhen the bit HOLDCNT (EQEI_CTL[24]) goes from low to high, the CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) is copied into CNTHOLD (EQEI_CNTHOLD[31:0]) register.
BitField.name: CNTHOLD

BitField.description: Enhanced Quadrature Encoder Interface Counter Index Latch\nWhen the IDXF (EQEI_STATUS[0]) bit is set, the CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) is copied into CNTLATCH (EQEI_CNTLATCH[31:0]) register.
BitField.name: CNTLATCH

BitField.name: CNTCMP

BitField.description: Hold EQEI_CNT Control\nWhen this bit is set from low to high, the CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) is copied into CNTHOLD(EQEI_CNTHOLD[31:0]). This bit may be set by writing 1 to it or Timer0~Timer3 interrupt flag TIF (TIMERx_INTSTS[0]). \nNote: This bit is automatically cleared after EQEI_CNTHOLD holds EQEI_CNT value.
BitField.name: HOLDCNT

BitField.description: Index Latch EQEI_CNT Enable Bit\nIf this bit is set to high, the CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) content will be latched into CNTLATCH (EQEI_CNTLATCH[31:0]) at every rising on signal CHX.
BitField.name: IDXLATEN

BitField.description: Index Trigger EQEI_CNT Reload Enable Bit
BitField.name: IDXRLDEN

BitField.description: The Compare Function Enable Bit\nThe compare function in EQEI controller is to compare the dynamic counting EQEI_CNT with the compare register CNTCMP( EQEI_CNTCMP[31:0]), if CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) reaches CNTCMP( EQEI_CNTCMP[31:0]), the flag CMPF will be set.
BitField.name: CMPEN

BitField.name: EQEIEN

BitField.name: SWAPEN

BitField.name: CRS

BitField.name: UTEN

BitField.name: UTHOLDEN

BitField.name: UTEVTRST

BitField.name: IDXRSTUTS

BitField.name: PHEIEN

BitField.description: UTIEF Trigger EQEI Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: UTIEIEN

BitField.description: Unit Timer Counter \nA 32-bit unit timer counter which may be reset to an initial value when any of the following events occur:
BitField.name: UTCNT

BitField.description: Unit Timer Counter Compare
BitField.name: UTCMP

BitField.description: IDX Detected Flag\nWhen the EQEI controller detects a rising edge on signal CHX it will set flag IDXF to high.\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: IDXF

BitField.description: Compare-match Flag\nIf the EQEI compare function is enabled, the flag is set by hardware while EQEI counter up or down counts and reach to the CNTCMP(EQEI_CNTCMP[31:0]).\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: CMPF

BitField.description: EQEI Counter Overflow or Underflow Flag\nFlag is set by hardware while CNT(EQEI_CNT[31:0]) overflows from 0xFFFF_FFFF to 0 in free-counting mode or from the CNTMAX (EQEI_CNTMAX[31:0]) to 0 in compare-counting mode. Similarly, the flag is set while EQEI counter underflows from 0 to 0xFFFF_FFFF or CNTMAX (EQEI_CNTMAX[31:0]).\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: OVUNF

BitField.description: Direction Change Flag\nFlag is set by hardware while EQEI counter counting direction is changed. Software can clear this bit by writing 1 to it.\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: DIRCHGF

BitField.description: EQEI Counter Counting Direction Indication\nNote: This bit is set/reset by hardware according to the phase detection between CHA and CHB.
BitField.name: DIRF

BitField.description: First IDX Signal Reset Event Flag (Read Only)
BitField.name: FIDXEF

BitField.description: EQEI Phase Error Flag\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: PHEF

BitField.description: EQEI Unit Timer Event Flag\nNote: This bit is only cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: UTIEF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nSetting this bit will enable the WDT time-out reset function If the WDT up counter value has not been cleared after the specific WDT reset delay period expires.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: RSTEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Reset Flag\nThis bit indicates the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset or not.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: RSTF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Flag\nThis bit will set to 1 while WDT up counter value reaches the selected WDT time-out interval.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: IF

BitField.description:
WDT Time-out Wake-up Function Control (Write Protect)
If this bit is set to 1, while WDT time-out interrupt flag IF (WDT_CTL[3]) is generated to 1 and interrupt enable bit INTEN (WDT_CTL[6]) is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal will generate a wake-up trigger event to chip.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
Note 2: Chip can be woken up by WDT time-out interrupt signal generated only if WDT clock source is selected to 10 kHz internal low speed RC oscillator (LIRC) or LXT.
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Wake-up Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt wake-up flag status of WDT\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: WKF

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nIf this bit is enabled, the WDT time-out interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: WDT Enable Bit (Write Protect)\nNote 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.\nNote 2: If CWDTEN[2:0] (combined by Config0[31] and Config0[4:3]) bits is not configured to 111, this bit is forced as 1 and user cannot change this bit to 0.
BitField.name: WDTEN

BitField.description: WDT Time-out Interval Selection (Write Protect)\nThese four bits select the time-out interval period for the WDT.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: TOUTSEL

BitField.description: WDT Enable Control SYNC Flag Indicator (Read Only)\nIf user executes enable/disable WDTEN (WDT_CTL[7]), this flag can be indicated enable/disable WDTEN function is completed or not.\nNote: Performing enable or disable WDTEN bit needs 4 * WDT_CLK period to become active.
BitField.name: SYNC

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit (Write Protect)\nWDT up counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.\nNote: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description:
WDT Reset Delay Selection (Write Protect)
When WDT time-out happened, user has a time named WDT Reset Delay Period to clear WDT counter by programming 0x5AA5 to prevent WDT time-out reset happened. User can select a suitable setting of RSTDSEL for different WDT Reset Delay Period.
Note 1: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
Note 2: This register will be reset to 0 if WDT time-out reset happened.
BitField.name: RSTDSEL

BitField.description: WDT Reset Counter Register\nWriting 0x00005AA5 to this field will reset the internal 20-bit WDT up counter value to 0.\nNote: Performing RSTCNT to reset counter needs 2 * WDT_CLK period to become active.
BitField.name: RSTCNT

BitField.description: WWDT Reload Counter Register\nWriting 0x00005AA5 to this register will reload the WWDT counter value to 0x3F.\nNote: User can only write WWDT_RLDCNT register to reload WWDT counter value when current WWDT counter value between 0 and CMPDAT (WWDT_CTL[21:16]). If user writes WWDT_RLDCNT when current WWDT counter value is larger than CMPDAT, WWDT reset signal will be generated immediately.
BitField.name: RLDCNT

BitField.description: WWDT Enable Bit
BitField.name: WWDTEN

BitField.description: WWDT Interrupt Enable Bit\nIf this bit is enabled, the WWDT counter compare match interrupt signal is generated and inform to CPU.
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: WWDT Counter Prescale Period Selection
BitField.name: PSCSEL

BitField.description: WWDT Window Compare\nSet this register to adjust the valid reload window. \nNote: User can only write WWDT_RLDCNT register to reload WWDT counter value when current WWDT counter value between 0 and CMPDAT. If user writes WWDT_RLDCNT register when current WWDT counter value larger than CMPDAT, WWDT reset signal will generate immediately.
BitField.name: CMPDAT

BitField.description: ICE Debug Mode Acknowledge Disable Bit\nWWDT down counter will keep going no matter CPU is held by ICE or not.
BitField.name: ICEDEBUG

BitField.description: WWDT Compare Match Interrupt Flag\nThis bit indicates the interrupt flag status of WWDT while WWDT counter value matches CMPDAT (WWDT_CTL[21:16]).\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: WWDTIF

BitField.description: WWDT Timer-out Reset Flag\nThis bit indicates the system has been reset by WWDT time-out reset or not.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: WWDTRF

BitField.description: WWDT Counter Value\nCNTDAT will be updated continuously to monitor 6-bit WWDT down counter value.
BitField.name: CNTDAT

BitField.description: RTC Active Status (Read Only)
BitField.name: ACTIVE

BitField.description: RTC Initiation (Write Only)\nWhen RTC block is powered on, RTC is at reset state. User has to write a number (0x a5eb1357) to INIT to make RTC leave reset state. Once the INIT is written as 0xa5eb1357, the RTC will be in un-reset state permanently.\nThe INIT is a write-only field and read value will be always 0.
BitField.name: INIT

BitField.description:
Tamper 0 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER0 detected level non-equal TAMP0LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[9]).
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP0IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 1 or Pair 0 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER1 detected level non-equal TAMP1LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[13]) or TAMPER0 and TAMPER1 disconnected during DYNPR0EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[15]) is activated.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP1IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 2 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER2 detected level non-equal TAMP2LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[17]).
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP2IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 3 or Pair 1 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER3 detected level non-equal TAMP3LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[21]) or TAMPER2 and TAMPER3 disconnected during DYNPR1EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[23]) is activated or TAMPER0 and TAMPER3 disconnected during DYNPR1EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[23]) and DYN1ISS (RTC_TAMPCTL[0]) are activated.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP3IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 4 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER4 detected level non-equal TAMP4LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[25]).
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP4IF

BitField.description:
Tamper 5 or Pair 2 Interrupt Flag
This bit is set when TAMPER5 detected level non-equal TAMP5LV (RTC_TAMPCTL[29]) or TAMPER4 and TAMPER5 disconnected during DYNPR2EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[31]) is activated or TAMPER0 and TAMPER5 disconnected during DYNPR2EN (RTC_TAMPCTL[31]) and DYN2ISS (RTC_TAMPCTL[1]) are activated.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit.
Note 2: This interrupt flag will generate again when Tamper setting condition is not restoration.
Note 3: Need to clear all TAMPxIF, after that, new RTC_TAMPTIME and RTC_TAMPCAL values can loaded while a tamper event occurred.
BitField.name: TAMP5IF

BitField.description: I/O Pin Backup Control Selection\nWhen low speed 32 kHz oscillator is disabled or TAMPxEN is disabled, PF.4 pin (X32_OUT pin), PF.5 pin (X32_IN pin) or PF.6~11 pin (TAMPERx pin) can be used as GPIO function. User can program IOCTLSEL to decide PF.4~11 I/O function is controlled by system power domain GPIO module or VBAT power domain RTC_GPIOCTL0/1 control register.\nNote: This bit field will be set to 1 by hardware automatically while the system entering Power-down mode if any writable RTC register has been written when RTCCKEN (CLK_APBCLK0[1]) enabled. And this bit field will keep 1 after the system wakes up, need to program it to 0 if want PF.4~11 I/O function is controlled by system power domain GPIO module.

BitField.description:
Reload New Seed for PRNG Engine

Note 1: Before this bit is set, the tamper configuration should be set to complete and this bit will be auto clear to 0 after reload new seed completed.
Note 2: The detection reference clock is RTC counter clock. Tamper detector needs to sync 2 ~ 3 RTC counter clock.

BitField.description:
Packet Scaling Horizontal Factor M
Specify the lower 8-bit of denominator part (M) of the horizontal scaling factor.
The lower 8-bit will be cascaded with higher 8-bit (PKDSHMH) to form a 16-bit denominator (M) of vertical factor.
The output image width will be equal to the image width * N/M.
Note: The value of N must be equal to or less than M.
BitField.name: PKTSHML

BitField.description: Packet Scaling Horizontal Factor N\nSpecify the lower 8-bit of numerator part (N) of the horizontal scaling factor.\nThe lower 8-bit will be cascaded with higher 8-bit (PKDSHNH) to form a 16-bit numerator of horizontal factor.
BitField.name: PKTSHNL

BitField.description:
Packet Scaling Vertical Factor M
Specify the lower 8-bit of denominator part (M) of the vertical scaling factor.
The lower 8-bit will be cascaded with higher 8-bit (PKDSVMH) to form a 16-bit denominator (M) of vertical factor.
The output image width will be equal to the image height * N/M.
Note: The value of N must be equal to or less than M.
BitField.name: PKTSVML

BitField.description: Packet Scaling Vertical Factor N\nSpecify the lower 8-bit of numerator part (N) of the vertical scaling factor. \nThe lower 8-bit will be cascaded with higher 8-bit (PKDSVNH) to form a 16-bit numerator of vertical factor.
BitField.name: PKTSVNL

BitField.description:
Scaling Frame Rate Factor M
Specify the denominator part (M) of the frame rate scaling factor.
The output image frame rate will be equal to input image frame rate * (N/M).
Note: The value of N must be equal to or less than M.
BitField.name: FRM

BitField.description: Scaling Frame Rate Factor N\nSpecify the numerator part (N) of the frame rate scaling factor.
BitField.name: FRN

Register.description: Frame Output Pixel Stride Width Register
Register.name: CCAP_STRIDE

BitField.description: Packet Frame Output Pixel Stride Width\nThe output pixel stride size of the packet pipe.\nIt is a 32-pixel aligned stride width for the Luma-Y-One bit format or a 4-pixel aligned stride with for the Luma-Y-Eight bit format when color or monochrome CMOS sensors used. This means that every new captured line is by word alignment address when color or monochrome CMOS sensors used.
BitField.name: PKTSTRIDE

BitField.description: Packet Scaling Horizontal Factor M\nSpecify the higher 8-bit of denominator part (M) of the horizontal scaling factor.\nPlease refer to the register 'CCAP_PKTSL' for the detailed operation.
BitField.name: PKTSHMH

BitField.description: Packet Scaling Horizontal Factor N\nSpecify the higher 8-bit of numerator part (N) of the horizontal scaling factor.\nPlease refer to the register 'CCAP_PKTSL' for the detailed operation.
BitField.name: PKTSHNH

BitField.description: Packet Scaling Vertical Factor M\nSpecify the higher 8-bit of denominator part (M) of the vertical scaling factor.\nPlease refer to the register 'CCAP_PKTSL' to check the cooperation between these two registers.

BitField.description: Function Mode\nThis bit field selects the protocol for this USCI controller. Selecting a protocol that is not available or a reserved combination disables the USCI. When switching between two protocols, the USCI has to be disabled before selecting a new protocol. Simultaneously, the USCI will be reset when user write 000 to FUNMODE.
BitField.name: FUNMODE

BitField.description: Transmit Start Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a transmit start event.
BitField.name: TXSTIEN

BitField.description: Transmit End Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a transmit finish event.
BitField.name: TXENDIEN

BitField.description: Receive Start Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a receive start event.
BitField.name: RXSTIEN

BitField.description: Receive End Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a receive finish event.
BitField.name: RXENDIEN

BitField.description: Reference Clock Source Selection\nThis bit selects the source signal of reference clock (fREF_CLK).
BitField.name: RCLKSEL

BitField.description: Protocol Clock Source Selection\nThis bit selects the source signal of protocol clock (fPROT_CLK).
BitField.name: PTCLKSEL

BitField.description: Sample Clock Source Selection\nThis bit field used for the clock source selection of a sample clock (fSAMP_CLK) for the protocol processor.
BitField.name: SPCLKSEL

BitField.description: Timing Measurement Counter Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the 10-bit timing measurement counter.
BitField.name: TMCNTEN

BitField.description: Timing Measurement Counter Clock Source Selection
BitField.name: TMCNTSRC

BitField.description: Pre-divider for Sample Counter
BitField.name: PDSCNT

BitField.description: Denominator for Sample Counter\nThis bit field defines the divide ratio of the sample clock fSAMP_CLK.\nNote: The maximum value of DSCNT is 0xF on UART mode and suggest to set over 4 to confirm the receiver data is sampled in right value.
BitField.name: DSCNT

BitField.description: Clock Divider\nNote: In UART function, it can be updated by hardware in the 4th falling edge of the input data 0x55 when the auto baud rate function (ABREN(UUART_PROTCTL[6])) is enabled. The revised value is the average bit time between bit 5 and bit 6. The user can use revised CLKDIV and new BRDETITV (UUART_PROTCTL[24:16]) to calculate the precise baud rate.
BitField.name: CLKDIV

Register.description: USCI Input Data Signal Configuration Register 0
Register.name: UUART_DATIN0

BitField.description: Input Signal Synchronization Selection\nThis bit selects if the un-synchronized input signal (with optionally inverted) or the synchronized (and optionally filtered) signal can be used as input for the data shift unit.
BitField.name: SYNCSEL

BitField.description: Input Signal Inverse Selection\nThis bit defines the inverter enable of the input asynchronous signal.
BitField.name: ININV

BitField.description: Input Signal Edge Detection Mode\nThis bit field selects which edge actives the trigger event of input data signal.\nNote: In UART function mode, it is suggested to set this bit field as 0x2.
BitField.name: EDGEDET

Register.description: USCI Input Control Signal Configuration Register 0
Register.name: UUART_CTLIN0

BitField.description: Input Synchronization Signal Selection\nThis bit selects if the un-synchronized input signal (with optionally inverted) or the synchronized (and optionally filtered) signal can be used as input for the data shift unit.
BitField.name: SYNCSEL

BitField.description: Input Signal Inverse Selection\nThis bit defines the inverter enable of the input asynchronous signal.
BitField.name: ININV

Register.description: USCI Input Clock Signal Configuration Register
Register.name: UUART_CLKIN

BitField.description: Input Synchronization Signal Selection\nThis bit selects if the un-synchronized input signal or the synchronized (and optionally filtered) signal can be used as input for the data shift unit.
BitField.name: SYNCSEL

BitField.description: LSB First Transmission Selection
BitField.name: LSB

BitField.description: Data Output Inverse Selection\nThis bit defines the relation between the internal shift data value and the output data signal of USCIx_DAT1 pin.
BitField.name: DATOINV

BitField.description: Control Signal Output Inverse Selection\nThis bit defines the relation between the internal control signal and the output control signal.\nNote: In UART protocol, the control signal means nRTS signal.
BitField.name: CTLOINV

BitField.description: Word Length of Transmission\nThis bit field defines the data word length (amount of bits) for reception and transmission. The data word is always right-aligned in the data buffer. USCI support word length from 4 to 16 bits.\nNote: In UART protocol, the length can be configured as 6~13 bits.
BitField.name: DWIDTH

BitField.description: Transmit Data\nSoftware can use this bit field to write 16-bit transmit data for transmission.
BitField.name: TXDAT

BitField.description: Received Data\nThis bit field monitors the received data which stored in receive data buffer.\nNote: RXDAT[15:13] indicate the same frame status of BREAK, FRMERR and PARITYERR (UUART_PROTSTS[7:5]).
BitField.name: RXDAT

BitField.description: Clear Transmit Buffer \nNote: It is cleared automatically after one PCLK cycle.
BitField.name: TXCLR

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Overrun Error Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: RXOVIEN

BitField.description: Clear Receive Buffer\nNote: It is cleared automatically after one PCLK cycle.
BitField.name: RXCLR

BitField.description: Transmit Reset\nNote: It is cleared automatically after one PCLK cycle.
BitField.name: TXRST

BitField.description: Receive Reset\nNote 1: It is cleared automatically after one PCLK cycle.\nNote 2: It is suggested to check the RXBUSY (UUART_PROTSTS[10]) before this bit will be set to 1.
BitField.name: RXRST

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Empty Indicator
BitField.name: RXEMPTY

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Full Indicator
BitField.name: RXFULL

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Over-run Error Interrupt Status\nThis bit indicates that a receive buffer overrun error event has been detected. If RXOVIEN (UUART_BUFCTL[14]) is enabled, the corresponding interrupt request is activated. It is cleared by software writes 1 to this bit.
BitField.name: RXOVIF

BitField.description: Transmit Buffer Empty Indicator
BitField.name: TXEMPTY

BitField.description: Transmit Buffer Full Indicator
BitField.name: TXFULL

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: PDMA Transmit Channel Available
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Receive Channel Available
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: PDMAEN

BitField.description: Wake-up Enable Bit
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Power Down Blocking Option
BitField.name: PDBOPT

BitField.description: Wake-up Flag\nWhen chip is woken up from Power-down mode, this bit is set to 1. Software can write 1 to clear this bit.
BitField.name: WKF

BitField.description: STOP bits\nThis bit defines the number of STOP bits in an UART frame.
BitField.name: STOPB

BitField.description: Parity Enable Bit\nThis bit defines the PARITY bit is enabled in an UART frame.
BitField.name: PARITYEN

BitField.description: Even Parity Enable Bit\nNote: This bit has effect only when PARITYEN is set.
BitField.name: EVENPARITY

BitField.description: nRTS Auto-flow Control Enable Bit\nNote: This bit has effect only when the RTSAUDIREN is not set.
BitField.name: RTSAUTOEN

BitField.description: nCTS Auto-flow Control Enable Bit\nWhen nCTS auto-flow is enabled, the UART will send data to external device when nCTS input assert (UART will not send data to device if nCTS input is dis-asserted).
BitField.name: CTSAUTOEN

BitField.description:
nRTS Auto Direction Enable Bit
When nRTS auto direction is enabled, if the transmitted bytes in the TX buffer is empty, the UART asserted nRTS signal automatically.
Note 1: This bit is used for nRTS auto direction control for RS485.
Note 2: This bit has effect only when the RTSAUTOEN is not set.
BitField.name: RTSAUDIREN

BitField.description: Auto-baud Rate Detect Enable Bit\nNote: When the auto - baud rate detect operation finishes, hardware will clear this bit. The associated interrupt ABRDETIF (UUART_PROTST[9]) will be generated (If ARBIEN (UUART_PROTIEN [1]) is enabled).
BitField.name: ABREN

BitField.description: Data Wake-up Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: DATWKEN

BitField.description: nCTS Wake-up Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: CTSWKEN

BitField.description: Wake-up Counter\nThese bits field indicate how many clock cycle selected by fPDS_CNT do the slave can get the 1st bit (START bit) when the device is wake-up from Power-down mode.
BitField.name: WAKECNT

BitField.description: Baud Rate Detection Interval \nThis bit fields indicate how many clock cycle selected by TMCNTSRC (UUART_BRGEN [5]) does the slave calculates the baud rate in one bits. The order of the bus shall be 1 and 0 step by step (e.g. the input data pattern shall be 0x55). The user can read the value to know the current input baud rate of the bus whenever the ABRDETIF (UUART_PROTCTL[9]) is set.\nNote: This bit can be cleared to 0 by software writing '0' to the BRDETITV.
BitField.name: BRDETITV

BitField.description: Stick Parity Enable Bit\nNote: Refer to RS-485 Support section for detailed information.
BitField.name: STICKEN

BitField.description: Transmit Break Control Enable Bit\nNote: When this bit is set to logic 1, the serial data output (TX) is forced to the Spacing State (logic 0). This bit acts only on TX line and has no effect on the transmitter logic.
BitField.name: BCEN

BitField.description: Deglitch Enable Bit\nNote 1: When this bit is set to logic 1, any pulse width less than about 150 ns will be considered a glitch and will be removed in the serial data input (RX). This bit acts only on RX line and has no effect on the transmitter logic.\nNote 2: It is recommended to set this bit only when operating at baud rate under 2.5 Mbps.
BitField.name: DGE

BitField.description: UART Protocol Enable Bit
BitField.name: PROTEN

BitField.description: Auto-baud Rate Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: ABRIEN

BitField.description: Receive Line Status Interrupt Enable Bit\nNote: UUART_PROTSTS[7:5] indicates the current interrupt event for receive line status interrupt.
BitField.name: RLSIEN

BitField.description: Transmit Start Interrupt Flag\nNote 1: It is cleared by software writing one into this bit.\nNote 2: Used for user to load next transmit data when there is no data in transmit buffer.
BitField.name: TXSTIF

BitField.description: Transmit End Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software writing 1 into this bit.
BitField.name: TXENDIF

BitField.description: Receive Start Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software writing 1 into this bit.
BitField.name: RXSTIF

BitField.description: Receive End Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software writing 1 into this bit.
BitField.name: RXENDIF

BitField.description: Parity Error Flag\nThis bit is set to logic 1 whenever the received character does not have a valid 'PARITY bit'.\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing '1' among the BREAK, FRMERR and PARITYERR bits.
BitField.name: PARITYERR

BitField.description: Framing Error Flag\nThis bit is set to logic 1 whenever the received character does not have a valid 'STOP bit' (that is, the STOP bit following the last data bit or PARITY bit is detected as logic 0).\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing '1' among the BREAK, FRMERR and PARITYERR bits.
BitField.name: FRMERR

BitField.description: Break Flag\nThis bit is set to logic 1 whenever the received data input (RX) is held in the 'spacing state' (logic 0) for longer than a full word transmission time (that is, the total time of 'START bit' + data bits + parity + STOP bits).\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing '1' among the BREAK, FRMERR and PARITYERR bits.
BitField.name: BREAK

BitField.description: Auto-baud Rate Interrupt Flag \nThis bit is set when auto-baud rate detection is done among the falling edge of the input data. If the ABRIEN (UUART_PROTCTL[6]) is set, the auto-baud rate interrupt will be generated. This bit can be set 4 times when the input data pattern is 0x55 and it is cleared before the next falling edge of the input bus.\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: ABRDETIF

BitField.description: RX Bus Status Flag (Read Only) \nThis bit indicates the busy status of the receiver.
BitField.name: RXBUSY

BitField.description:
Auto-baud Rate Error Status 
This bit is set when auto-baud rate detection counter overrun. When the auto-baud rate counter overrun, the user shall revise the CLKDIV (UUART_BRGEN[25:16]) value and enable ABREN (UUART_PROTCTL[6]) to detect the correct baud rate again.
Note 1: This bit is set at the same time of ABRDETIF.
Note 2: This bit can be cleared by writing '1' to ABRDETIF or ABERRSTS.
BitField.name: ABERRSTS

BitField.description: nCTS Synchronized Level Status (Read Only)\nThis bit used to indicate the current status of the internal synchronized nCTS signal.
BitField.name: CTSSYNCLV

BitField.description: nCTS Pin Status (Read Only)\nThis bit used to monitor the current status of nCTS pin input.
BitField.name: CTSLV

BitField.description: Function Mode\nThis bit field selects the protocol for this USCI controller. Selecting a protocol that is not available or a reserved combination disables the USCI. When switching between two protocols, the USCI has to be disabled before selecting a new protocol. Simultaneously, the USCI will be reset when user write 000 to FUNMODE.\nNote: Other bit combinations are reserved.
BitField.name: FUNMODE

BitField.description: Transmit Start Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a transmit start event.\nNote: The transmit start event happens when hardware starts to move TX data from data buffer to shift data unit.
BitField.name: TXSTIEN

BitField.description: Transmit End Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a transmit finish event.\nNote: The transmit finish event happens when hardware sends the last bit of TX data from shift data unit.
BitField.name: TXENDIEN

BitField.description: Receive Start Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a receive start event.\nNote: For SPI master mode, the receive start event happens when SPI master sends slave select active and spi clock to the external SPI slave. For SPI slave mode, the receive start event happens when slave select of SPI slave is active and spi clock of SPI slave is inputed from the external SPI master.
BitField.name: RXSTIEN

BitField.description: Receive End Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a receive finish event.\nNote: The receive finish event happens when hardware receives the last bit of RX data into shift data unit.
BitField.name: RXENDIEN

BitField.description: Reference Clock Source Selection\nThis bit selects the source of reference clock (fREF_CLK).
BitField.name: RCLKSEL

BitField.description: Protocol Clock Source Selection\nThis bit selects the source of protocol clock (fPROT_CLK).
BitField.name: PTCLKSEL

BitField.description: Sample Clock Source Selection\nThis bit field used for the clock source selection of sample clock (fSAMP_CLK) for the protocol processor.
BitField.name: SPCLKSEL

BitField.description: Time Measurement Counter Enable Bit\nThis bit enables the 10-bit timing measurement counter.
BitField.name: TMCNTEN

BitField.description: Time Measurement Counter Clock Source Selection
BitField.name: TMCNTSRC

BitField.description: Clock Divider
BitField.name: CLKDIV

BitField.name: SYNCSEL

BitField.name: SYNCSEL

BitField.description:
Word Length of Transmission
This bit field defines the data word length (amount of bits) for reception and transmission. The data word is always right-aligned in the data buffer. USCI support word length from 4 to 16 bits.
0x0: The data word contains 16 bits located at bit positions [15:0].
0x1: Reserved.
0x2: Reserved.
0x3: Reserved.
0x4: The data word contains 4 bits located at bit positions [3:0].
0x5: The data word contains 5 bits located at bit positions [4:0].
...
0xF: The data word contains 15 bits located at bit positions [14:0].
BitField.name: DWIDTH

BitField.description: Transmit Data\nSoftware can use this bit field to write 16-bit transmit data for transmission. In order to avoid overwriting the transmit data, user have to check TXEMPTY (USPI_BUFSTS[8]) status before writing transmit data into this bit field.

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Full Indicator
BitField.name: RXFULL

BitField.description: Receive Buffer Over-run Interrupt Status\nThis bit indicates that a receive buffer overrun event has been detected. If RXOVIEN (USPI_BUFCTL[14]) is enabled, the corresponding interrupt request is activated. It is cleared by software writes 1 to this bit.
BitField.name: RXOVIF

BitField.description: Transmit Buffer Empty Indicator
BitField.name: TXEMPTY

BitField.description: Transmit Buffer Full Indicator
BitField.name: TXFULL

BitField.description: Transmit Buffer Under-run Interrupt Status\nThis bit indicates that a transmit buffer under-run event has been detected. If enabled by TXUDRIEN (USPI_BUFCTL[6]), the corresponding interrupt request is activated. It is cleared by software writes 1 to this bit
BitField.name: TXUDRIF

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: PDMA Transmit Channel Available
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Receive Channel Available
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: PDMAEN

BitField.description: Wake-up Enable Bit
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: Power Down Blocking Option
BitField.name: PDBOPT

BitField.description: Wake-up Flag\nWhen chip is woken up from Power-down mode, this bit is set to 1. Software can write 1 to clear this bit.
BitField.name: WKF

BitField.description: Slave Mode Selection
BitField.name: SLAVE

BitField.description: Slave 3-wire Mode Selection for Slave Only\nThe SPI protocol can work with 3-wire interface (without slave select signal) in Slave mode.
BitField.name: SLV3WIRE

BitField.description: Slave Select Control for Master Only\nIf AUTOSS bit is cleared, setting this bit to 1 will set the slave select signal to active state, and setting this bit to 0 will set the slave select back to inactive state.\nNote: In SPI protocol, the internal slave select signal is active high.
BitField.name: SS

BitField.description: Automatic Slave Select Function Enable for Master Only
BitField.name: AUTOSS

BitField.description: Serial Bus Clock Mode\nThis bit field defines the SCLK idle status, data transmit, and data receive edge.
BitField.name: SCLKMODE

BitField.description:
Suspend Interval for Master Only
This bit field provides the configurable suspend interval between two successive transmit/receive transaction in a transfer. The definition of the suspend interval is the interval between the last clock edge of the preceding transaction word and the first clock edge of the following transaction word. The default value is 0x3. The period of the suspend interval is obtained according to the following equation.
 (SUSPITV[3:0] + 0.5) * period of SPI_CLK clock cycle
Example:
BitField.name: SUSPITV

BitField.description:
Transmit Data Mode Selection
This bit field describes how receive and transmit data is shifted in and out.
Other values are reserved.
Note: Changing the value of this bit field will produce the TXRST and RXRST to clear the TX/RX data buffer automatically.
BitField.name: TSMSEL

BitField.description: Slave Mode Time-out Period for Slave Only\nIn Slave mode, this bit field is used for Slave time-out period. This bit field indicates how many clock periods (selected by TMCNTSRC, USPI_BRGEN[5]) between the two edges of input SCLK will assert the Slave time-out event. Writing 0x0 into this bit field will disable the Slave time-out function.\nExample: Assume SLVTOCNT is 0x0A and TMCNTSRC (USPI_BRGEN[5]) is 1, it means the time-out event will occur if the state of SPI bus clock pin is not changed more than (10+1) periods of fDIV_CLK.
BitField.name: SLVTOCNT

BitField.description: Transmit Under-run Data Polarity for Slave\nThis bit defines the transmitting data value of USCIx_DAT1 when no data is available for transferring.
BitField.name: TXUDRPOL

BitField.description: SPI Protocol Enable Bit
BitField.name: PROTEN

BitField.description: Slave Select Inactive Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables/disables the generation of a slave select interrupt if the slave select changes to inactive.
BitField.name: SSINAIEN

BitField.description: Slave Select Active Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis bit enables/disables the generation of a slave select interrupt if the slave select changes to active.
BitField.name: SSACTIEN

BitField.description: Slave Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit\nIn SPI protocol, this bit enables the interrupt generation in case of a Slave time-out event.
BitField.name: SLVTOIEN

BitField.description: Slave Mode Bit Count Error Interrupt Enable Bit\nIf data transfer is terminated by slave time-out or slave select inactive event in Slave mode, so that the transmit/receive data bit count does not match the setting of DWIDTH (USPI_LINECTL[11:8]). Bit count error event occurs.
BitField.name: SLVBEIEN

BitField.description: Transmit Start Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software write 1 to this bit. The transmit start event happens when hardware starts to move TX data from data buffer to shift data unit.
BitField.name: TXSTIF

BitField.description: Transmit End Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software write 1 to this bit. The transmit end event happens when hardware sends the last bit of TX data from shift data unit.
BitField.name: TXENDIF

BitField.description: Receive Start Interrupt Flag\nNote: It is cleared by software write 1 to this bit. For SPI master mode, the receive start event happens when SPI master sends slave select active and spi clock to the external SPI slave.
