Note: In Master mode, QSPI controller will start to transfer the QSPI bus clock after 1 APB clock and 6 peripheral clock cycles after user writes to this register.
BitField.name: TX

BitField.description: Data Receive RegisterThere are 8-level FIFO buffers in this controller The data receive register holds the data received from QSPI data input pin If the RXEMPTY (QSPIx_STATUS[8) is not set to 1, the receive FIFO buffers can be accessed through software by reading this register(Read Only)
BitField.name: RX

BitField.description: QSPI Transfer Control Enable Bit\nIn Master mode, the transfer will start when there is data in the FIFO buffer after this bit is set to 1. In Slave mode, this device is ready to receive data when this bit is set to 1.\nNote: Before changing the configurations of QSPIx_CTL, QSPIx_CLKDIV, QSPIx_SSCTL and QSPIx_FIFOCTL registers, user shall clear the SPIEN (QSPIx_CTL[0]) and confirm the SPIENSTS (QSPIx_STATUS[15]) is 0.
BitField.name: SPIEN

BitField.description: Receive on Negative Edge
BitField.name: RXNEG

BitField.description: Transmit on Negative Edge\nNote: In TX DTR mode, TXNEG equals to CLKPOL (QSPIx_CTL[3]).
BitField.name: TXNEG

BitField.description: Clock Polarity
BitField.name: CLKPOL

BitField.description:
Suspend Interval
The four bits provide configurable suspend interval between two successive transmit/receive transaction in a transfer. The definition of the suspend interval is the interval between the last clock edge of the preceding transaction word and the first clock edge of the following transaction word. The default value is 0x3. The period of the suspend interval is obtained according to the following equation (Master only).
 (SUSPITV[3:0] + 0.5) * period of QSPI_CLK clock cycle
Example:
Note: In TX DTR mode, SUSPITV equals to 0x0.
BitField.name: SUSPITV

BitField.description: Data Width\nThis field specifies how many bits can be transmitted/received in one transaction. The minimum bit length is 8 bits and can up to 32 bits.
BitField.name: DWIDTH

BitField.description: Send LSB First
BitField.name: LSB

BitField.description: QSPI Half-duplex Transfer Enable Bit\nThis bit is used to select full-duplex or half-duplex for QSPI transfer. The bit field DATDIR (QSPIx_CTL[20]) can be used to set the data direction in half-duplex transfer.
BitField.name: HALFDPX

BitField.description: Receive-only Mode Enable Bit\nThis bit field is only available in Master mode. In receive-only mode, QSPI Master will generate QSPI bus clock continuously for receiving data bit from SPI slave device and assert the BUSY status. (Master Only)
BitField.name: RXONLY

BitField.description: 2-bit Transfer Mode Enable Bit\nNote: When 2-bit Transfer mode is enabled, the first serial transmitted bit data is from the first FIFO buffer data, and the 2nd serial transmitted bit data is from the second FIFO buffer data. As the same as transmitted function, the first received bit data is stored into the first FIFO buffer and the 2nd received bit data is stored into the second FIFO buffer at the same time.
BitField.name: TWOBIT

BitField.description: Unit Transfer Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: UNITIEN

BitField.description: Slave Mode Control
BitField.name: SLAVE

BitField.description: Byte Reorder Function Enable Bit\nNote: Byte Reorder function is only available if DWIDTH is defined as 16, 24, and 32 bits.
BitField.name: REORDER

BitField.description: Data Port Direction Control\nThis bit is used to select the data input/output direction in half-duplex transfer and Dual/Quad transfer
BitField.name: DATDIR

BitField.description: Dual I/O Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: DUALIOEN

BitField.description: Quad I/O Mode Enable Bit
BitField.name: QUADIOEN

BitField.description: Transmit Double Transfer Rate Mode Enable Bit\nNote: QSPI Master mode supports TXDTR mode, and QSPI Slave mode does not support this mode.
BitField.name: TXDTREN

BitField.description:
Clock Divider
The value in this field is the frequency divider for generating the peripheral clock, fspi_eclk, and the QSPI bus clock of QSPI Master. The frequency is obtained according to the following equation.

where 
 is the peripheral clock source, which is defined in the clock control register, CLK_CLKSEL2.
Note: The time interval must be larger than or equal to 8 peripheral clock cycles between releasing QSPI IP software reset and setting this clock divider register.
BitField.name: DIVIDER

BitField.description:
Slave Selection Control
If AUTOSS bit is cleared to 0,
Note: This function is Master only.


Note
BitField.name: SS

BitField.description: Slave Selection Active Polarity\nThis bit defines the active polarity of slave selection signal (QSPIx_SS).
BitField.name: SSACTPOL

BitField.description: Automatic Slave Selection Function Enable BitThis bit is supported in Master mode only
BitField.name: AUTOSS

BitField.description: Slave 3-wire Mode Enable Bit\nIn Slave 3-wire mode, the QSPI controller can work with 3-wire interface including QSPIx_CLK, QSPIx_MISO and QSPIx_MOSI pins.
BitField.name: SLV3WIRE

BitField.description: Slave Mode Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SLVTOIEN

BitField.description: Slave Mode Time-out Reset Control
BitField.name: SLVTORST

BitField.description: Slave Mode Bit Count Error Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SLVBEIEN

BitField.description: Slave Mode TX Under Run Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SLVURIEN

BitField.description: Slave Select Active Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SSACTIEN

BitField.description: Slave Select Inactive Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SSINAIEN

BitField.description: Slave Mode Time-out Period\nIn Slave mode, these bits indicate the time-out period when there is bus clock input during slave select active. The clock source of the time-out counter is Slave peripheral clock. If the value is 0, it indicates the slave mode time-out function is disabled.
BitField.name: SLVTOCNT

BitField.description: Transmit PDMA Enable Bit\nNote 1: In QSPI Master mode with full duplex transfer, if both TX and RX PDMA functions are enabled, RX PDMA function cannot be enabled prior to TX PDMA function. User can enable TX PDMA function firstly or enable both functions simultaneously.\nNote 2: In QSPI Master mode with full duplex transfer, if both TX and RX PDMA functions are enabled, TX PDMA function cannot be disabled prior to RX PDMA function. User can disable RX PDMA function firstly or disable both functions simultaneously.
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: Receive PDMA Enable Bit
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: Receive Reset
BitField.name: RXRST

BitField.description: Transmit Reset\nNote: If TX underflow event occurs in QSPI Slave mode, this bit can be used to make QSPI return to idle state.
BitField.name: TXRST

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Threshold Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: RXTHIEN

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Threshold Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: TXTHIEN

BitField.description: Receive Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: RXTOIEN

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Overrun Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: RXOVIEN

BitField.description: TX Underflow Data Polarity\nNote 1: The TX underflow event occurs if there is no any data in TX FIFO when the slave selection signal is active.\nNote 2: When TX underflow event occurs, QSPIx_MISO pin state will be determined by this setting even though TX FIFO is not empty afterward. Data stored in TX FIFO will be sent through QSPIx_MISO pin in the next transfer frame.
BitField.name: TXUFPOL

BitField.description: TX Underflow Interrupt Enable Bit\nWhen TX underflow event occurs in Slave mode, TXUFIF (QSPIx_STATUS[19]) will be set to 1. This bit is used to enable the TX underflow interrupt.
BitField.name: TXUFIEN

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Buffer Clear\nNote: The RX shift register will not be cleared.
BitField.name: RXFBCLR

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Buffer Clear\nNote: The TX shift register will not be cleared.
BitField.name: TXFBCLR

BitField.description: RX FIFO Write Data Enable Bit When Slave Mode Bit Count Error
BitField.name: SLVBERX

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Threshold\nIf the valid data count of the receive FIFO buffer is larger than the RXTH setting, the RXTHIF bit will be set to 1, else the RXTHIF bit will be cleared to 0.
BitField.name: RXTH

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Threshold\nIf the valid data count of the transmit FIFO buffer is less than or equal to the TXTH setting, the TXTHIF bit will be set to 1, else the TXTHIF bit will be cleared to 0.
BitField.name: TXTH

BitField.description: Busy Status (Read Only)\nNote: By applications, this QSPI busy flag should be used with other status registers in QSPIx_STATUS such as TXCNT, RXCNT, TXTHIF, TXFULL, TXEMPTY, RXTHIF, RXFULL, RXEMPTY, and UNITIF. Therefore the QSPI transfer done events of TX/RX operations can be obtained at correct timing point.
BitField.name: BUSY

BitField.description: Unit Transfer Interrupt Flag\nNote: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: UNITIF

BitField.description: Slave Select Active Interrupt Flag\nNote: Only available in Slave mode. This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SSACTIF

BitField.description: Slave Select Inactive Interrupt Flag\nNote: Only available in Slave mode. This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SSINAIF

BitField.description: Slave Select Line Bus Status (Read Only)\nNote: This bit is only available in Slave mode. If SSACTPOL (QSPIx_SSCTL[2]) is set 0, and the SSLINE is 1, the QSPI slave select is in inactive status.
BitField.name: SSLINE

BitField.description: Slave Time-out Interrupt Flag \nWhen the slave select is active and the value of SLVTOCNT is not 0, if the bus clock is detected, the slave time-out counter in QSPI controller logic will be started. When the value of time-out counter is greater than or equal to the value of SLVTOCNT (QSPIx_SSCTL[31:16]) before one transaction is done, the slave time-out interrupt event will be asserted.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SLVTOIF

BitField.description: Slave Mode Bit Count Error Interrupt Flag\nIn Slave mode, when the slave select line goes to inactive state, if bit counter is mismatch with DWIDTH, this interrupt flag will be set to 1.\nNote: If the slave select active but there is no any bus clock input, the SLVBEIF also active when the slave select goes to inactive state. This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SLVBEIF

BitField.description: Slave Mode TX Under Run Interrupt Flag\nIn Slave mode, if TX underflow event occurs and the slave select line goes to inactive state, this interrupt flag will be set to 1.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SLVURIF

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Buffer Empty Indicator (Read Only)
BitField.name: RXEMPTY

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Buffer Full Indicator (Read Only)
BitField.name: RXFULL

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Threshold Interrupt Flag (Read Only)
BitField.name: RXTHIF

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Overrun Interrupt Flag\nWhen the receive FIFO buffer is full, the follow-up data will be dropped and this bit will be set to 1.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: RXOVIF

BitField.description: Receive Time-out Interrupt Flag\nNote: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: RXTOIF

BitField.description: QSPI Enable Status (Read Only)\nNote: The QSPI peripheral clock is asynchronous with the system clock. In order to make sure the QSPI control logic is disabled, this bit indicates the real status of QSPI controller.
BitField.name: SPIENSTS

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Buffer Empty Indicator (Read Only)
BitField.name: TXEMPTY

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Buffer Full Indicator (Read Only)
BitField.name: TXFULL

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Threshold Interrupt Flag (Read Only)
BitField.name: TXTHIF

BitField.description:
TX Underflow Interrupt Flag
When the TX underflow event occurs, this bit will be set to 1, the state of data output pin depends on the setting of TXUFPOL.
Note 1: This bit will be cleared by writing 1 to it.
Note 2: If reset slave's transmission circuit when slave selection signal is active, this flag will be set to 1 after 2 peripheral clock cycles + 3 system clock cycles since the reset operation is done.
BitField.name: TXUFIF

BitField.description: TX or RX Reset Status (Read only)\nNote: Both the reset operations of TXRST and RXRST need 3 system clock cycles + 2 peripheral clock cycles. User can check the status of this bit to monitor the reset function is doing or done.
BitField.name: TXRXRST

BitField.description: Receive FIFO Data Count (Read only)\nThis bit field indicates the valid data count of receive FIFO buffer.
BitField.name: RXCNT

BitField.description: Transmit FIFO Data Count (Read only)\nThis bit field indicates the valid data count of transmit FIFO buffer.
BitField.name: TXCNT

BitField.description:
Effective Bit Number of Uncompleted RX Data
This status register indicates that effective bit number of uncompleted RX data when SLVBERX (QSPIx_FIFOCTL[10]) is enabled and RX bit count error event happen in QSPI slave mode.
This status register will be fixed to 0x0 when SLVBERX (QSPIx_FIFOCTL[10]) is disabled.
Note: This register will be cleared to 0x0 when user write 0x1 to SLVBEIF (QSPIx_STATUS[6]).
BitField.name: SLVBENUM

BitField.description:
Data Transmit Register
The data transmit registers pass through the transmitted data into the 8-level transmit FIFO buffers. The number of valid bits depends on the setting of DWIDTH (QSPIx_CTL[12:8]) in QSPI mode.
In QSPI mode, if DWIDTH is set to 0x08, the bits TX[7:0] will be transmitted. If DWIDTH is set to 0x00, the QSPI controller will perform a 32-bit transfer.
Note: In Master mode, QSPI controller will start to transfer the QSPI bus clock after 1 APB clock and 6 peripheral clock cycles after user writes to this register.
BitField.name: TX

BitField.description: Data Receive RegisterThere are 8-level FIFO buffers in this controller The data receive register holds the data received from QSPI data input pin If the RXEMPTY (QSPIx_STATUS[8) is not set to 1, the receive FIFO buffers can be accessed through software by reading this register(Read Only)
BitField.name: RX

BitField.description: Cipher Disable Bit
BitField.name: CIPHOFF

BitField.description: Balance the AHB Control Time Between Cipher Enable and Disable Control\nWhen cipher is enabled, the AHB control signal will delay some time caused by the encoding or decoding calculation. Therefore, if setting BALEN to 1, it will make the AHB signal processing time with cipher disabled be equal to that with cipher enabled.\nNote: Only useful when cipher is disabled.
BitField.name: BALEN

BitField.description: 4-byte Address Mode Enable Bit\nNote: Used for DMA write mode, DMA read mode, and DMM mode.
BitField.name: B4ADDREN

BitField.description: Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: IEN

BitField.description: Interrupt Flag\nWrite Operation:
BitField.name: IF

BitField.description:
Transmit/Receive Bit Length
This specifies how many bits are transmitted/received in one transmit/receive transaction.
Note 1: Only used for normal I/O mode.
Note 2: Only 8, 16, 24, and 32 bits are allowed. Other bit length will result in incorrect transfer.
BitField.name: DWIDTH

BitField.description: Transmit/Receive Burst Number\nThis field specifies how many transmit/receive transactions should be executed continuously in one transfer.\nNote: Only used for normal I/O Mode.
BitField.name: BURSTNUM

BitField.description: SPI Interface Direction Select for Quad and Dual Mode Only\nNote: Only used for normal I/O mode.
BitField.name: QDIODIR

BitField.description: Suspend Interval\nNote: Only used for normal I/O mode.
BitField.name: SUSPITV

BitField.description: SPI Interface Bit Mode\nNote: Only used for normal I/O mode.
BitField.name: BITMODE

BitField.description:
SPI Function Operation Mode
Note 1: After using Normal I/O mode of SPI Flash controller to program the content of external SPI Flash, please set CDINVAL(SPIM_CTL1[3]) to 0x1 (Set all cache data to be invalid).
Note 2: In DMA write mode, hardware will send just one page program command per operation. Users must take care of cross-page cases. After using DMA write mode of SPI Flash controller to program the content of external SPI Flash, please set CDINVAL(SPIM_CTL1[3]) to 0x1 (Set all cache data to be invalid).
Note 3: For external SPI Flash with 32 Mbytes, access address range of external SPI Flash address is from 0x00000000 to 0x01FFFFFF when using Normal I/O mode, DMA write mode, and DMA read mode to write/read external SPI Flash data. Please user check size of used SPI Flash component to know access address range of external SPI Flash.
Note 4: For external SPI Flash with 32 Mbytes, access address range of external SPI Flash address is from 0x08000000 to 0x09FFFFFF when using Direct Memory mapping mode (DMM mode) to read external SPI Flash data. Please user check size of used SPI Flash component to know access address range of external SPI Flash.
BitField.name: OPMODE

BitField.description:
Page Program Command Code
The Others command codes are Reserved.
The DTR read commands '0x0D,0xBD,0xED' improves throughput by transferring address and data on both the falling and rising edge of SPI Flash clock (SPIM_CLK). It is similar to those commands '0x0B, 0xBB, 0xEB' but allows transfer of address and data on rising edge and falling edge of SPI Flash output clock. (Note2)
Note 1: Quad mode of SPI Flash must be enabled first by normal I/O mode before using quad page program/quad read commands.
Note 2: See SPI Flash specifications for support items.
Note 3: For TYPE_1, TYPE_2, and TYPE_3 of page program command code, refer to Figure 6.294, Figure 6.295, and Figure 6.296.
Note 4: Please disable 'continuous read mode' and 'burst wrap mode' before DMA write mode of SPI Flash controller is used to program data of external SPI Flash. After using DMA write mode of SPI Flash controller to program the content of external SPI Flash, please set CDINVAL(SPIM_CTL1[3]) to 0x1 (Set all cache data to be invalid).
BitField.name: CMDCODE

BitField.description: Go and Busy Status\nWrite Operation:\nNote: All registers should be set before writing 1 to the SPIMEN bit. When a transfer is in progress, user should not write to any register of this peripheral.
BitField.name: SPIMEN

BitField.description: Cache Memory Function Disable Bit
BitField.name: CACHEOFF

BitField.description:
Cache Data Invalid Enable Bit
Write Operation:
Read Operation: No effect
Note: When SPI Flash memory is page erasing or whole Flash erasing, please set CDINVAL to 0x1. After using normal I/O mode or DMA write mode of SPI Flash controller to program or erase the content of external SPI Flash, please set CDINVAL to 0x1.
BitField.name: CDINVAL

BitField.description: Slave Select Active Enable Bit\nNote: This interface can only drive one device/slave at a given time. Therefore, the slave selects of the selected device must be set to its active level before starting any read or write transfer. Functional description of SSACTPOL(SPIM_CTL1[5]) and SS is shown in Table 6.291.
BitField.name: SS

BitField.description: Slave Select Active Level\nIt defines the active level of device/slave select signal (SPIM_SS), as shown in Table 6.291.
BitField.name: SSACTPOL

BitField.description: Idle Time Interval\nIn DMM mode, IDLETIME is set to control the minimum idle time between two SPI Flash accesses.
BitField.name: IDLETIME

BitField.description:
Clock Divider Register
The value in this field is the frequency divider of the AHB clock (HCLK) to generate the serial SPI output clock 'SCLK' on the output SPIM_CLK pin. The desired frequency is obtained according to the following equation:

Note 1: When set DIVIDER to zero, the frequency of SPIM_CLK will be equal to the frequency of HCLK.
Note 2: SCLK is serial SPI output clock.
Note 3: Each SPI Flash command has the limitation of the maximum operation frequency of SCLK. Please check the specification of the used SPI Flash component to decide the frequency of SPI Flash clock for different command operations of SPI Flash.
Note 4: For DTR read commands '0x0D, 0xBD, 0xED', the setting values of DIVIDER are only all multiples of 2. For example, 1,2,4,8,16,32,...
BitField.name: DIVIDER

BitField.description: SPI Flash Deselect Time Interval of DMA Write Mode for DMA Write Mode Only\nThe bits set the deselect time interval of SPI Flash (i.e. time interval of inactive level of SPIM_SS) when SPI Flash controller operates on DMA write mode. (Note1)
BitField.name: DWDELSEL

BitField.description: SPI Flash Phase Delay Time for DMA Write Mode and DMA Read Mode Only\nThe bits set phase delay time between command data phase, address data phase, and dummy cycle phase, where SPI Flash controller will send those phase data to external SPI Flash.
BitField.name: PHDELSEL

BitField.description:
Sampling Clock Delay Selection for Received Data for Normal I/O Mode, DMA Read Mode, DMA Write Mode, and Direct Memory Mapping Mode Only
Determine the number of inserted delay cycles. Used to adjust the sampling clock of received data to latch the correct data.
0x0: No delay. (Default)
0x1: Delay 1 SPI Flash clock.
0x2: Delay 2 SPI Flash clocks.
0x3: Delay 3 SPI Flash clocks.
...
0x7: Delay 7 SPI Flash clocks
Note: The manufacturer or device ID of external SPI Flash component can be used to determine the correct setting value of RDDLYSEL. An example is given as follows.
For example, the manufacturer ID and device ID of external SPI Flash for some vendor are 0xEF and 0x1234 separately. First, set RDDLYSEL to 0x0, and use read manufacturer id/device id command to read the manufacturer id of external SPI Flash by using normal I/O mode (the manufacturer id is 0xEF (1110_1111) in this example).
If the manufacturer ID which reads from external SPI Flash is 0xF7 (1111_0111), it denotes that manufacturer id is shifted the right by 1 bit and most significant bit (MSB) of manufacturer id is assigned to 1. According to manufacturer id reads from external SPI Flash, RDDLYSEL needs to be set to 0x1 to receive SPI Flash data correctly.
BitField.name: RDDLYSEL

BitField.description: Sampling Clock Edge Selection of Received Data for Normal I/O Mode, DMA Read Mode, DMA Write Mode, and Direct Memory Mapping Mode Only
BitField.name: RDEDGE

BitField.description:
Data Receive Register
The Data Receive Registers hold the received data of the last executed transfer. 
Number of valid RX registers is specified in SPIM_CTL0[BURSTNUM]. If BURSTNUM 0, received data are held in the most significant RXDAT register first.
Number of valid-bit is specified in SPIM_CTL0[DWIDTH]. If DWIDTH is 16, 24, or 32, received data are held in the least significant byte of RXDAT register first.
In a byte, received data are held in the most significant bit of RXDAT register first.
BitField.name: RXDAT

BitField.description:
Data Transmit Register
The Data Transmit Registers hold the data to be transmitted in next transfer. 
Number of valid TXDAT registers is specified in SPIM_CTL0[BURSTNUM]. If BURSTNUM 0, data are transmitted in the most significant TXDAT register first.
Number of valid-bit is specified in SPIM_CTL0[DWIDTH]. If DWIDTH is 16, 24, or 32, data are transmitted in the least significant byte of TXDAT register first.
In a byte, data are transmitted in the most significant bit of TXDAT register first.
BitField.name: TXDAT

BitField.description:
SRAM Memory Address
For DMA Read mode, this is the destination address for DMA transfer.
For DMA Write mode, this is the source address for DMA transfer.
Note: This address must be word-aligned.
BitField.name: ADDR

BitField.description:
DMA Transfer Byte Count Register
It indicates the transfer length for DMA process. 
Note 1: The unit for counting is byte.
Note 2: The number must be the multiple of 4.
Note 3: Please check specification of used SPI Flash to know maximum byte length of page program.
BitField.name: DMACNT

BitField.description:
SPI Flash Address Register
For DMA Read mode, this is the source address for DMA transfer.
For DMA Write mode, this is the destination address for DMA transfer.
Note 1: This address must be word-aligned.
Note 2: For external SPI Flash with 32 Mbytes, the value of this SPI Flash address register 'ADDR' is from 0x00000000 to 0x00FFFFFF when using DMA write mode and DMA read mode to write/read external SPI Flash data. Please user check size of used SPI Flash component to know access address range of external SPI Flash.
BitField.name: ADDR

BitField.description:
Cipher Key1 Register
This is the KEY1 data for cipher function.
Note 1: If there is not any KEY1(SPIM_KEY1[31:0]) or KEY2(SPIM_KEY2[31:0]) (KEY1 is 0x0000_0000 or KEY2 is 0x0000_0000), the cipher function will be disabled automatically.
Note 2: When CIPHOFF(SPIM_CTL0[0]) is 0, both of KEY1(SPIM_KEY1[31:0]) and KEY2(SPIM_KEY2[31:0]) do not equal to 0x0000_0000 (i.e. KEY1 0x0000_0000 and KEY20x0000_0000), cipher encryption/decryption is enabled.
BitField.name: KEY1

BitField.description:
Cipher Key2 Register
This is the KEY2 data for cipher function.
Note 1: If there is not any KEY1(SPIM_KEY1[31:0]) or KEY2(SPIM_KEY2[31:0]) (KEY1 is 0x0000_0000 or KEY2 is 0x0000_0000), the cipher function will be disabled automatically.
Note 2: When CIPHOFF(SPIM_CTL0[0]) is 0, both of KEY1(SPIM_KEY1[31:0]) and KEY2(SPIM_KEY2[31:0]) do not equal to 0x0000_0000 (i.e. KEY1 0x0000_0000 and KEY20x0000_0000), cipher encryption/decryption is enabled.
BitField.name: KEY2

Register.description: Direct Memory Mapping Mode Control Register
Register.name: SPIM_DMMCTL

BitField.description:
Mode Bits Data for Continuous Read Mode for Direct Memory Mapping Mode Only
Set the mode bits data for continuous read mode (or performance enhance mode).
When setting this mode bits currently (Note1) and set CREN(SPIM_DMMCTL[25]), this reduces the command phase by eight clocks and allows the read address to be immediately entered after SPIM_SS asserted to active. (Note1)
Note 1: Please check the used SPI Flash specification to know the setting value of this mode bits data, and different SPI Flash vendor may use different setting values.
Note 2: CRMDAT needs to be used with CREN(SPIM_DMMCTL[25]).
BitField.name: CRMDAT

BitField.description:
SPI Flash Deselect Time for Direct Memory Mapping Mode Only
Set the minimum time width of SPI Flash deselect time (i.e. Minimum SPIM_SS deselect time), as shown in Figure 6.293.
(1) Cache function disable:
Note 3: Please check the used SPI Flash specification to know the setting value of this register, and different SPI Flash vendor may use different setting values.
BitField.name: DESELTIM

BitField.description: 16 Bytes Burst Wrap Mode Enable Bit for Direct Memory Mapping Mode, Cache Enable, and Read Command Code 0xEB, and 0xE7 Only\nIn direct memory mapping mode, both of quad read commands '0xEB' and '0xE7' support burst wrap mode for cache application and performance enhance. For cache application, the burst wrap mode can be used to fill the cache line quickly (In this SPI Flash controller, use cache data line with 16 bytes size). For performance enhance with direct memory mapping mode and cache enable, when cache data is miss, the burst wrap mode can let MCU get the required SPI Flash data quickly.\nNote: In Direct Memory Mapping Mode, the cache function needs to be enabled when 16 bytes burst wrap mode is enabled.
BitField.name: BWEN

BitField.description: Continuous Read Mode Enable Bit for Direct Memory Mapping Mode, Read Command Codes 0xBB, 0xEB, 0xE7, 0x0D, 0xBD, and 0xED Only\nFor read operations of SPI Flash, commands of fast read quad I/O (0xEB), word read quad I/O (0xE7), fast read dual I/O (0xBB), DTR fast read (0x0D), DTR fast read dual I/O (0xBD), and DTR fast read quad I/O (0xED) can further reduce command overhead through setting the 'continuous read mode' bits (8 bits) after the input address data.\nNote: When using function of continuous read mode and setting USETEN (SPIM_CTL2[16]) to 1, CRMDAT(SPIM_DMMCTL[15:8]) must be set by used SPI Flash specifications. When using function of continuous read mode and setting USETEN(SPIM_CTL2[16]) to 0, CRMDAT(SPIM_DMMCTL[15:8]) is set to value 0x20.
BitField.name: CREN

BitField.description: User Sets SPI Flash Active SCLK Time for Direct Memory Mapping Mode, DMA Write Mode, and DMA Read Mode Only\nNote: When user wants to set ACTSCLKT(SPIM_DMMCTL[31:28]) manually, please set UACTSCLK to 1.
BitField.name: UACTSCLK

BitField.description:
SPI Flash Active SCLK Time for Direct Memory Mapping Mode, DMA Write Mode, and DMA Read Mode Only
The bits set time interval between SPIM SS active edge and the position edge of the first serial SPI output clock, as shown in Figure 6.293.
Note 2: SCLK is SPI output clock
Note 3: Please check the used SPI Flash specification to know the setting value of this register, and different SPI Flash vendor may use different setting values.
BitField.name: ACTSCLKT

BitField.description: User Set Value Enable Bit for Direct Memory Mapping Mode and DMA Read Mode with Read Commands 0x03,0x0B,0x3B,0xBB,0xEB, and 0xE7 Only\nFor DTR command codes 0x0D, 0xBD, and 0xED, please set USETEN to 0x1.
BitField.name: USETEN

BitField.description: Mode Phase OFF for DTR Command Codes 0x0D, 0xBD, and 0xED for Direct Memory Mapping Mode and DMA Read Mode Only\nNote: Please check the used SPI Flash specification to know the mode cycle number (or performance enhance cycle number) for DTR command codes 0x0D, 0xBD, and 0xED.
BitField.name: DTRMPOFF

BitField.description:
Dummy Cycle Number for Direct Memory Mapping Mode and DMA Read Mode Only
Set number of dummy cycles
(1) For non-DTR command codes 0x03, 0x0B, 0x3B, 0xBB, 0xEB, and 0xE7:
For command codes 0x0B, 0x3B, 0xEB, and 0xE7, user only set DCNUM to dummy cycle number by used SPI Flash specification.
(2) For DTR command codes 0x0D, 0xBD, and 0xED:
user sets DCNUM to dummy cycle number and DTRMPOFF(SPIM_CTL2[20]) by used SPI Flash specification.
Note: Number of dummy cycles depends on the frequency of SPI output clock, SPI Flash vendor, and read command types. Please check the used SPI Flash specification to know the setting value of this number of dummy cycles.
BitField.name: DCNUM

BitField.description: Assert Acknowledge Control
BitField.name: AA

BitField.description: I2C Interrupt Flag\nWhen a new I2C state is present in the I2C_STATUS0 register, the SI flag is set by hardware. If bit INTEN (I2C_CTL0 [7]) is set, the I2C interrupt is requested. SI must be cleared by software. Clear SI by writing 1 to this bit.\nFor ACKMEN is set in slave read mode, the SI flag is set in 8th clock period for user to confirm the acknowledge bit and 9th clock period for user to read the data in the data buffer.
BitField.name: SI

BitField.description: I2C STOP Control\nIn Master mode, setting STO to transmit a STOP condition to bus then I2C controller will check the bus condition if a STOP condition is detected. This bit will be cleared by hardware automatically.
BitField.name: STO

BitField.description: I2C START Control\nSetting STA to logic 1 to enter Master mode, the I2C hardware sends a START or repeat START condition to bus when the bus is free.
BitField.name: STA

BitField.description: I2C Controller Enable Bit
BitField.name: I2CEN

BitField.description: Enable Interrupt
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Data Phase Bit Count Select
BitField.name: DPBITSEL

BitField.description: Data Phase Count Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: DPCINTEN

BitField.description: Slave Read Command Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SRCINTEN

BitField.description: Data Phase Count Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when I2C transfer bit count equal to DPBITSEL setting \nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: DPCIF

BitField.description: Slave Address Read Command Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when I2C receive address match read command.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SARCIF

BitField.description: General Call Function
BitField.name: GC

BitField.description: I2C Address \nThe content of this register is irrelevant when I2C is in Master mode. In the slave mode, the seven most significant bits must be loaded with the chip's own address. The I2C hardware will react if either of the address is matched.\nNote: When software set 10'h000, the address cannot be used.
BitField.name: ADDR

BitField.description: I2C Data \nBit [7:0] is located with the 8-bit transferred/received data of I2C serial port.
BitField.name: DAT

BitField.description: I2C Status
BitField.name: STATUS

BitField.description: I2C Clock Divided \nNote: The minimum value of I2C_CLKDIV is 4.
BitField.name: DIVIDER

BitField.description: Noise Filter Count \nThe register bits control the input filter width.\nNote: Filter width Min :3*PCLK, Max : 18*PCLK
BitField.name: NFCNT

BitField.description: Time-out Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when I2C time-out happened and it can interrupt CPU if I2C interrupt enable bit (INTEN) is set to 1.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: TOIF

BitField.description: Time-out Counter Input Clock Divided by 4\nWhen enabled, the time-out period is extended 4 times.
BitField.name: TOCDIV4

BitField.description: Time-out Counter Enable Bit\nWhen enabled, the 14-bit time-out counter will start counting when SI is cleared. Setting flag SI to '1' will reset counter and re-start up counting after SI is cleared.
BitField.name: TOCEN

BitField.description: I2C Address Mask\nI2C bus controllers support multiple address recognition with four address mask register. When the bit in the address mask register is set to one, it means the received corresponding address bit is don't-care. If the bit is set to zero, that means the received corresponding register bit should be exact the same as address register.\nNote: The wake-up function cannot use address mask.
BitField.name: ADDRMSK

BitField.description: I2C Wake-up Enable Bit
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: I2C No Hold BUS Enable Bit\nNote: The I2C controller could respond when WKIF event is not clear, it may cause error data transmitted or received. If data transmitted or received when WKIF event is not clear, user must reset I2C controller and execute the original operation again.
BitField.name: NHDBUSEN

BitField.description: I2C Wake-up Flag\nWhen chip is woken up from Power-down mode by I2C, this bit is set to 1. \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: WKIF

BitField.description: Wakeup Address Frame Acknowledge Bit Done\nNote: This bit cannot release WKIF. This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: WKAKDONE

BitField.description: Read/Write Status Bit in Address Wakeup Frame\nNote: This bit will be cleared when software can write 1 to WKAKDONE bit.
BitField.name: WRSTSWK

BitField.description: PDMA Transmit Channel Available
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Receive Channel Available
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: I2C over Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting OVRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is over run event in received buffer.
BitField.name: OVRIEN

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting UDRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is under run event happened in transmitted buffer.
BitField.name: UDRIEN

BitField.description: Two-level BUFFER Enable Bit\nSet to enable the two-level buffer for I2C transmitted or received buffer. It is used to improve the performance of the I2C bus.
BitField.name: TWOBUFEN

BitField.description: PDMA Stretch Bit
BitField.name: PDMASTR

BitField.description: Address 10-bit Function Enable Bit
BitField.name: ADDR10EN

BitField.description: SCL And SDA Pin Switch Enable Bit\nNote: Original pin configuration table is shown in Basic Configuration section.
BitField.name: SWITCHEN

BitField.description: I2C Address 0 Match Status\nWhen address 0 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT0

BitField.description: I2C Address 1 Match Status\nWhen address 1 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT1

BitField.description: I2C Address 2 Match Status\nWhen address 2 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT2

BitField.description: I2C Address 3 Match Status\nWhen address 3 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1, and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT3

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER FULL (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 2.
BitField.name: FULL

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER EMPTY (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 0.
BitField.name: EMPTY

BitField.description: I2C over Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: OVR

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: UDR

BitField.description: On Bus Busy (Read Only)\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected.
BitField.name: ONBUSY

BitField.description: Setup Time Configure Control\nThis field is used to generate a delay timing between SDA falling edge and SCL rising edge in transmission mode.\nNote: Setup time setting should not make SCL output less than three PCLKs.
BitField.name: STCTL

BitField.description: Hold Time Configure Control \nThis field is used to generate the delay timing between SCL falling edge and SDA rising edge in transmission mode.
BitField.name: HTCTL

BitField.description: Acknowledge Control by Manual\nIn order to allow ACK control in slave reception including the command and data, slave byte control mode must be enabled by setting the ACKMEN bit.
BitField.name: ACKMEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Calculation Enable Bit\nNote: When I2C enter power-down mode, the bit should be enabled after wake-up if needed PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Device Default Address Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMDEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Host Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMHEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Alert Enable Bit
BitField.name: ALERTEN

BitField.description: Suspend/Control Data Output Status
BitField.name: SCTLOSTS

BitField.description: Suspend or Control Pin Output Enable Bit
BitField.name: SCTLOEN

BitField.description: BUS Enable Bit\nNote: When the bit is enabled, the internal 14-bit counter is used to calculate the time out event of clock low condition.
BitField.name: BUSEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transmission/Reception
BitField.name: PECTXEN

BitField.description: Timer Check in Idle State\nThe BUSTOCHK is used to calculate the time-out of clock low in bus active and the idle period in bus Idle. This bit is used to define which condition is enabled.\nNote: The BUSY (I2C_BUSSTS[0]) indicates the current bus state.
BitField.name: BUSTOCHK

BitField.description: PEC Clear at Repeat Start\nThe calculation of PEC starts when PECEN is set to 1 and it is cleared when the STA or STO bit is detected. This PECCLR bit is used to enable the condition of REPEAT START can clear the PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECCLR

BitField.description: Acknowledge Manual Enable Extra SI Interrupt
BitField.name: ACKM9SI

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Count Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BCDIEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transfer Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: PECDIEN

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Timer Control Register
Register.name: I2C_BUSTCTL

BitField.description: Bus Time Out Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOEN

BitField.description: Cumulative Clock Low Time Out Enable Bit\nFor Master, it calculates the period from START to ACK\nFor Slave, it calculates the period from START to STOP
BitField.name: CLKTOEN

BitField.description: Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOIEN

BitField.description: Extended Clock Time Out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CLKTOIEN

BitField.description: Time Out Reset Enable Bit
BitField.name: TORSTEN

BitField.description: Bus Busy\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected
BitField.name: BUSY

BitField.description: Byte Count Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BCDONE

BitField.description: PEC Error in Reception \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECERR

BitField.description: SMBus Alert Status \nNote: 1. The SMBALERT pin is an open-drain pin, the pull-high resistor is must in the system. 2. This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ALERT

BitField.description: Bus Suspend or Control Signal Input Status
BitField.name: SCTLDIN

BitField.description: Bus Time-out Status \nIn bus busy, the bit indicates the total clock low time-out event occurred; otherwise, it indicates the bus idle time-out event occurred.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BUSTO

BitField.description: Clock Low Cumulate Time-out Status \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: CLKTO

BitField.description: PEC Byte Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECDONE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Number Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTSIZE

BitField.description: Transfer Byte Number\nThe transmission or receive byte number in one transaction when the PECEN is set. The maximum transaction or receive byte is 256 Bytes.\nNote: The byte number counting includes address, command code, and data frame.
BitField.name: PLDSIZE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Value Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTCRC

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Value (Read Only)
BitField.name: PECCRC

BitField.description: Bus Management Time-out Value\nIndicates the bus time-out value in bus is IDLE or SCL low.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of BUSTOUT, the TORSTEN (I2C_BUSTCTL[4]) bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN(I2C_BUSCTL[7]) is set.

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Clock Low Timer Register
Register.name: I2C_CLKTOUT

BitField.description: Bus Clock Low Timer\nThe field is used to configure the cumulative clock extension time-out.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of CLKLTOUT, the TORSTEN bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN is set.

BitField.description: Slave Address Read Command Interrupt Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when I2C receive address match read command.\nNote: This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it.
BitField.name: SARCIF

BitField.description: General Call Function
BitField.name: GC

BitField.description: I2C Address \nThe content of this register is irrelevant when I2C is in Master mode. In the slave mode, the seven most significant bits must be loaded with the chip's own address. The I2C hardware will react if either of the address is matched.\nNote: When software set 10'h000, the address cannot be used.
BitField.name: ADDR

BitField.description: I2C Data \nBit [7:0] is located with the 8-bit transferred/received data of I2C serial port.
BitField.name: DAT

BitField.description: I2C Status
BitField.name: STATUS

BitField.description: I2C Clock Divided \nNote: The minimum value of I2C_CLKDIV is 4.
BitField.name: DIVIDER

BitField.description: Noise Filter Count \nThe register bits control the input filter width.\nNote: Filter width Min :3*PCLK, Max : 18*PCLK
BitField.name: NFCNT

BitField.description: Time-out Flag\nThis bit is set by hardware when I2C time-out happened and it can interrupt CPU if I2C interrupt enable bit (INTEN) is set to 1.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: TOIF

BitField.description: Time-out Counter Input Clock Divided by 4\nWhen enabled, the time-out period is extended 4 times.
BitField.name: TOCDIV4

BitField.description: Time-out Counter Enable Bit\nWhen enabled, the 14-bit time-out counter will start counting when SI is cleared. Setting flag SI to '1' will reset counter and re-start up counting after SI is cleared.
BitField.name: TOCEN

BitField.description: I2C Address Mask\nI2C bus controllers support multiple address recognition with four address mask register. When the bit in the address mask register is set to one, it means the received corresponding address bit is don't-care. If the bit is set to zero, that means the received corresponding register bit should be exact the same as address register.\nNote: The wake-up function cannot use address mask.
BitField.name: ADDRMSK

BitField.description: I2C Wake-up Enable Bit
BitField.name: WKEN

BitField.description: I2C No Hold BUS Enable Bit\nNote: The I2C controller could respond when WKIF event is not clear, it may cause error data transmitted or received. If data transmitted or received when WKIF event is not clear, user must reset I2C controller and execute the original operation again.
BitField.name: NHDBUSEN

BitField.description: I2C Wake-up Flag\nWhen chip is woken up from Power-down mode by I2C, this bit is set to 1. \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: WKIF

BitField.description: Wakeup Address Frame Acknowledge Bit Done\nNote: This bit cannot release WKIF. This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: WKAKDONE

BitField.description: Read/Write Status Bit in Address Wakeup Frame\nNote: This bit will be cleared when software can write 1 to WKAKDONE bit.
BitField.name: WRSTSWK

BitField.description: PDMA Transmit Channel Available
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Receive Channel Available
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: I2C over Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting OVRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is over run event in received buffer.
BitField.name: OVRIEN

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting UDRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is under run event happened in transmitted buffer.
BitField.name: UDRIEN

BitField.description: Two-level BUFFER Enable Bit\nSet to enable the two-level buffer for I2C transmitted or received buffer. It is used to improve the performance of the I2C bus.
BitField.name: TWOBUFEN

BitField.description: PDMA Stretch Bit
BitField.name: PDMASTR

BitField.description: Address 10-bit Function Enable Bit
BitField.name: ADDR10EN

BitField.description: SCL And SDA Pin Switch Enable Bit\nNote: Original pin configuration table is shown in Basic Configuration section.
BitField.name: SWITCHEN

BitField.description: I2C Address 0 Match Status\nWhen address 0 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT0

BitField.description: I2C Address 1 Match Status\nWhen address 1 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT1

BitField.description: I2C Address 2 Match Status\nWhen address 2 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT2

BitField.description: I2C Address 3 Match Status\nWhen address 3 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1, and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT3

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER FULL (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 2.
BitField.name: FULL

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER EMPTY (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 0.
BitField.name: EMPTY

BitField.description: I2C over Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: OVR

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: UDR

BitField.description: On Bus Busy (Read Only)\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected.
BitField.name: ONBUSY

BitField.description: Setup Time Configure Control\nThis field is used to generate a delay timing between SDA falling edge and SCL rising edge in transmission mode.\nNote: Setup time setting should not make SCL output less than three PCLKs.
BitField.name: STCTL

BitField.description: Hold Time Configure Control \nThis field is used to generate the delay timing between SCL falling edge and SDA rising edge in transmission mode.
BitField.name: HTCTL

BitField.description: Acknowledge Control by Manual\nIn order to allow ACK control in slave reception including the command and data, slave byte control mode must be enabled by setting the ACKMEN bit.
BitField.name: ACKMEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Calculation Enable Bit\nNote: When I2C enter power-down mode, the bit should be enabled after wake-up if needed PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Device Default Address Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMDEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Host Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMHEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Alert Enable Bit
BitField.name: ALERTEN

BitField.description: Suspend/Control Data Output Status
BitField.name: SCTLOSTS

BitField.description: Suspend or Control Pin Output Enable Bit
BitField.name: SCTLOEN

BitField.description: BUS Enable Bit\nNote: When the bit is enabled, the internal 14-bit counter is used to calculate the time out event of clock low condition.
BitField.name: BUSEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transmission/Reception
BitField.name: PECTXEN

BitField.description: Timer Check in Idle State\nThe BUSTOCHK is used to calculate the time-out of clock low in bus active and the idle period in bus Idle. This bit is used to define which condition is enabled.\nNote: The BUSY (I2C_BUSSTS[0]) indicates the current bus state.
BitField.name: BUSTOCHK

BitField.description: PEC Clear at Repeat Start\nThe calculation of PEC starts when PECEN is set to 1 and it is cleared when the STA or STO bit is detected. This PECCLR bit is used to enable the condition of REPEAT START can clear the PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECCLR

BitField.description: Acknowledge Manual Enable Extra SI Interrupt
BitField.name: ACKM9SI

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Count Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BCDIEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transfer Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: PECDIEN

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Timer Control Register
Register.name: I2C_BUSTCTL

BitField.description: Bus Time Out Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOEN

BitField.description: Cumulative Clock Low Time Out Enable Bit\nFor Master, it calculates the period from START to ACK\nFor Slave, it calculates the period from START to STOP
BitField.name: CLKTOEN

BitField.description: Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOIEN

BitField.description: Extended Clock Time Out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CLKTOIEN

BitField.description: Time Out Reset Enable Bit
BitField.name: TORSTEN

BitField.description: Bus Busy\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected
BitField.name: BUSY

BitField.description: Byte Count Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BCDONE

BitField.description: PEC Error in Reception \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECERR

BitField.description: SMBus Alert Status \nNote: 1. The SMBALERT pin is an open-drain pin, the pull-high resistor is must in the system. 2. This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ALERT

BitField.description: Bus Suspend or Control Signal Input Status
BitField.name: SCTLDIN

BitField.description: Bus Time-out Status \nIn bus busy, the bit indicates the total clock low time-out event occurred; otherwise, it indicates the bus idle time-out event occurred.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BUSTO

BitField.description: Clock Low Cumulate Time-out Status \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: CLKTO

BitField.description: PEC Byte Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECDONE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Number Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTSIZE

BitField.description: Transfer Byte Number\nThe transmission or receive byte number in one transaction when the PECEN is set. The maximum transaction or receive byte is 256 Bytes.\nNote: The byte number counting includes address, command code, and data frame.
BitField.name: PLDSIZE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Value Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTCRC

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Value (Read Only)
BitField.name: PECCRC

BitField.description: Bus Management Time-out Value\nIndicates the bus time-out value in bus is IDLE or SCL low.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of BUSTOUT, the TORSTEN (I2C_BUSTCTL[4]) bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN(I2C_BUSCTL[7]) is set.
BitField.name: BUSTO

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Clock Low Timer Register
Register.name: I2C_CLKTOUT

BitField.description: Bus Clock Low Timer\nThe field is used to configure the cumulative clock extension time-out.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of CLKLTOUT, the TORSTEN bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN is set.
BitField.name: CLKTO

BitField.description: Assert Acknowledge Control
BitField.name: AA

BitField.description: I2C Interrupt Flag\nWhen a new I2C state is present in the I2C_STATUS0 register, the SI flag is set by hardware. If bit INTEN (I2C_CTL0 [7]) is set, the I2C interrupt is requested. SI must be cleared by software. Clear SI by writing 1 to this bit.\nFor ACKMEN is set in slave read mode, the SI flag is set in 8th clock period for user to confirm the acknowledge bit and 9th clock period for user to read the data in the data buffer.
BitField.name: SI

BitField.description: I2C STOP Control\nIn Master mode, setting STO to transmit a STOP condition to bus then I2C controller will check the bus condition if a STOP condition is detected. This bit will be cleared by hardware automatically.
BitField.name: STO

BitField.description: I2C START Control\nSetting STA to logic 1 to enter Master mode, the I2C hardware sends a START or repeat START condition to bus when the bus is free.
BitField.name: STA

BitField.description: I2C Controller Enable Bit
BitField.name: I2CEN

BitField.description: Enable Interrupt
BitField.name: INTEN

BitField.description: Data Phase Bit Count Select
BitField.name: DPBITSEL

BitField.description: Data Phase Count Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: DPCINTEN

BitField.description: Slave Read Command Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: SRCINTEN

BitField.description: Read/Write Status Bit in Address Wakeup Frame\nNote: This bit will be cleared when software can write 1 to WKAKDONE bit.
BitField.name: WRSTSWK

BitField.description: PDMA Transmit Channel Available
BitField.name: TXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Receive Channel Available
BitField.name: RXPDMAEN

BitField.description: PDMA Reset
BitField.name: PDMARST

BitField.description: I2C over Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting OVRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is over run event in received buffer.
BitField.name: OVRIEN

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Interrupt Control Bit\nSetting UDRIEN to logic 1 will send a interrupt to system when the TWOFF bit is enabled and there is under run event happened in transmitted buffer.
BitField.name: UDRIEN

BitField.description: Two-level BUFFER Enable Bit\nSet to enable the two-level buffer for I2C transmitted or received buffer. It is used to improve the performance of the I2C bus.
BitField.name: TWOBUFEN

BitField.description: PDMA Stretch Bit
BitField.name: PDMASTR

BitField.description: Address 10-bit Function Enable Bit
BitField.name: ADDR10EN

BitField.description: SCL And SDA Pin Switch Enable Bit\nNote: Original pin configuration table is shown in Basic Configuration section.
BitField.name: SWITCHEN

BitField.description: I2C Address 0 Match Status\nWhen address 0 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT0

BitField.description: I2C Address 1 Match Status\nWhen address 1 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT1

BitField.description: I2C Address 2 Match Status\nWhen address 2 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1 and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT2

BitField.description: I2C Address 3 Match Status\nWhen address 3 is matched, hardware will inform which address used. This bit will be set to 1, and will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ADMAT3

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER FULL (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 2.
BitField.name: FULL

BitField.description: TWO-LEVEL BUFFER EMPTY (Read Only)\nThis bit is set when POINTER is equal to 0.
BitField.name: EMPTY

BitField.description: I2C over Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: OVR

BitField.description: I2C Under Run Status Bit (Read Only)
BitField.name: UDR

BitField.description: On Bus Busy (Read Only)\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected.
BitField.name: ONBUSY

BitField.description: Setup Time Configure Control\nThis field is used to generate a delay timing between SDA falling edge and SCL rising edge in transmission mode.\nNote: Setup time setting should not make SCL output less than three PCLKs.
BitField.name: STCTL

BitField.description: Hold Time Configure Control \nThis field is used to generate the delay timing between SCL falling edge and SDA rising edge in transmission mode.
BitField.name: HTCTL

BitField.description: Acknowledge Control by Manual\nIn order to allow ACK control in slave reception including the command and data, slave byte control mode must be enabled by setting the ACKMEN bit.
BitField.name: ACKMEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Calculation Enable Bit\nNote: When I2C enter power-down mode, the bit should be enabled after wake-up if needed PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Device Default Address Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMDEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Host Enable Bit
BitField.name: BMHEN

BitField.description: Bus Management Alert Enable Bit
BitField.name: ALERTEN

BitField.description: Suspend/Control Data Output Status
BitField.name: SCTLOSTS

BitField.description: Suspend or Control Pin Output Enable Bit
BitField.name: SCTLOEN

BitField.description: BUS Enable Bit\nNote: When the bit is enabled, the internal 14-bit counter is used to calculate the time out event of clock low condition.
BitField.name: BUSEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transmission/Reception
BitField.name: PECTXEN

BitField.description: Timer Check in Idle State\nThe BUSTOCHK is used to calculate the time-out of clock low in bus active and the idle period in bus Idle. This bit is used to define which condition is enabled.\nNote: The BUSY (I2C_BUSSTS[0]) indicates the current bus state.
BitField.name: BUSTOCHK

BitField.description: PEC Clear at Repeat Start\nThe calculation of PEC starts when PECEN is set to 1 and it is cleared when the STA or STO bit is detected. This PECCLR bit is used to enable the condition of REPEAT START can clear the PEC calculation.
BitField.name: PECCLR

BitField.description: Acknowledge Manual Enable Extra SI Interrupt
BitField.name: ACKM9SI

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Count Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BCDIEN

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Transfer Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: PECDIEN

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Timer Control Register
Register.name: I2C_BUSTCTL

BitField.description: Bus Time Out Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOEN

BitField.description: Cumulative Clock Low Time Out Enable Bit\nFor Master, it calculates the period from START to ACK\nFor Slave, it calculates the period from START to STOP
BitField.name: CLKTOEN

BitField.description: Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BUSTOIEN

BitField.description: Extended Clock Time Out Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CLKTOIEN

BitField.description: Time Out Reset Enable Bit
BitField.name: TORSTEN

BitField.description: Bus Busy\nIndicates that a communication is in progress on the bus. It is set by hardware when a START condition is detected. It is cleared by hardware when a STOP condition is detected
BitField.name: BUSY

BitField.description: Byte Count Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BCDONE

BitField.description: PEC Error in Reception \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECERR

BitField.description: SMBus Alert Status \nNote: 1. The SMBALERT pin is an open-drain pin, the pull-high resistor is must in the system. 2. This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: ALERT

BitField.description: Bus Suspend or Control Signal Input Status
BitField.name: SCTLDIN

BitField.description: Bus Time-out Status \nIn bus busy, the bit indicates the total clock low time-out event occurred; otherwise, it indicates the bus idle time-out event occurred.\nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: BUSTO

BitField.description: Clock Low Cumulate Time-out Status \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: CLKTO

BitField.description: PEC Byte Transmission/Receive Done \nNote: This bit will be cleared by software writing 1.
BitField.name: PECDONE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Number Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTSIZE

BitField.description: Transfer Byte Number\nThe transmission or receive byte number in one transaction when the PECEN is set. The maximum transaction or receive byte is 256 Bytes.\nNote: The byte number counting includes address, command code, and data frame.
BitField.name: PLDSIZE

Register.description: I2C Packet Error Checking Byte Value Register
Register.name: I2C_PKTCRC

BitField.description: Packet Error Checking Byte Value (Read Only)
BitField.name: PECCRC

BitField.description: Bus Management Time-out Value\nIndicates the bus time-out value in bus is IDLE or SCL low.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of BUSTOUT, the TORSTEN (I2C_BUSTCTL[4]) bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN(I2C_BUSCTL[7]) is set.
BitField.name: BUSTO

Register.description: I2C Bus Management Clock Low Timer Register
Register.name: I2C_CLKTOUT

BitField.description: Bus Clock Low Timer\nThe field is used to configure the cumulative clock extension time-out.\nNote: If the user wants to revise the value of CLKLTOUT, the TORSTEN bit shall be set to 1 and cleared to 0 first when the BUSEN is set.
BitField.name: CLKTO

BitField.description: SDH Shared Buffer\nSingle 128 Bytes shared buffer for data exchange between system memory and cards.
BitField.name: SB

BitField.description: DMA Engine Enable Bit\nNote 1: If this bit is cleared, DMA will ignore all requests from SD host and force bus master into IDLE state.\nNote 2: If target abort occurred, DMAEN will be cleared.
BitField.name: DMAEN

BitField.description: Software Engine Reset\nNote: The software reset DMA related registers.
BitField.name: DMARST

BitField.description: Scatter-gather Function Enable Bit
BitField.name: SGEN

BitField.description: DMA Transfer Is in Progress\nThis bit indicates if SD Host is granted and doing DMA transfer or not.
BitField.name: DMABUSY

BitField.description: Determined to the PAD Table Fetching Is in Order or Out of Order
BitField.name: ORDER

BitField.description:
DMA Transfer Starting Address
This field pads 0 as least significant bit indicates a 32-bit starting address of system memory (SRAM) for DMA to retrieve or fill in data.
If DMA is not in normal mode, this field will be interpreted as a starting address of Physical Address Descriptor (PAD) table.
Note: Starting address of the SRAM must be word aligned, for example, 0x0000_0000, 0x0000_0004.
BitField.name: DMASA

BitField.description: DMA Transfer Byte Count (Read Only)\nThis field indicates the remained byte count of DMA transfer. The value of this field is valid only when DMA is busy; otherwise, it is 0.
BitField.name: BCNT

BitField.description: DMA Read/Write Target Abort Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: ABORTIEN

BitField.description: Wrong EOT Encountered Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: WEOTIEN

BitField.description: DMA Read/Write Target Abort Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nNote 1: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.\nNote 2: When DMA's bus master received ERROR response, it means that target abort is happened. DMA will stop transfer and respond this event and then go to IDLE state. When target abort occurred or WEOTIF is set, software must reset DMA and SD host, and then transfer those data again.
BitField.name: ABORTIF

BitField.description: Wrong EOT Encountered Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nWhen DMA Scatter-Gather function is enabled, and EOT of the descriptor is encountered before DMA transfer finished (that means the total sector count of all PAD is less than the sector count of SD host), this bit will be set.\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: WEOTIF

BitField.description: Software Engine Reset
BitField.name: GCTLRST

BitField.description: Secure Digital Functionality Enable Bit
BitField.name: SDEN

BitField.description: DMA READ/WRITE Target Abort Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: DTAIEN

BitField.description: DMA READ/WRITE Target Abort Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates DMA received an ERROR response from internal AHB bus during DMA read/write operation. When Target Abort is occurred, please reset all engine.\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: DTAIF

BitField.description: Command Output Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: COEN

BitField.description: Response Input Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: RIEN

BitField.description: Data Input Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: DIEN

BitField.description: Data Output Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: DOEN

BitField.description: Response R2 Input Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: R2EN

BitField.description: Initial 74 Clock Cycles Output Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: CLK74OEN

BitField.description: Generating 8 Clock Cycles Output Enable Bit\nNote: When operation is finished, this bit will be cleared automatically, so don't write 0 to this bit (the controller will be abnormal).
BitField.name: CLK8OEN

BitField.description: SD Clock Enable Control
BitField.name: CLKKEEP

BitField.description: SD Command Code\nThe bits contain the SD command code (0x00 - 0x3F).
BitField.name: CMDCODE

BitField.description: Software Engine Reset
BitField.name: CTLRST

BitField.description: SD Data Bus Width Selection
BitField.name: DBW

BitField.description: Block Counts to Be Transferred or Received\nThis field contains the block counts for data-in and data-out transfer. For READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK and WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK command, software can use this function to accelerate data transfer and improve performance. Don't fill 0x0 to this field.\nNote: For READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK and WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK command, the actual total length is BLKCNT * (BLKLEN +1).
BitField.name: BLKCNT

BitField.description: NWR Parameter for Block Write Operation\nThis value indicates the NWR parameter for data block write operation in SD clock counts. The actual clock cycle will be SDNWR+1.
BitField.name: SDNWR

BitField.description: SD Command Argument\nThis register contains a 32-bit value specifies the argument of SD command from host controller to SD card. Before trigger COEN (SDH_CTL [0]), software should fill argument in this field.
BitField.name: ARGUMENT

BitField.description: Block Transfer Done Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: BLKDIEN

BitField.description: CRC7, CRC16 and CRC Status Error Interrupt Enable Bit
BitField.name: CRCIEN

BitField.description: SD Card Detection Interrupt Enable Bit\nEnable/Disable interrupts generation of SD controller when card is inserted or removed.
BitField.name: CDIEN

BitField.description: Response Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit\nEnable/Disable interrupts generation of SD controller when receiving response or R2 time-out. Time-out value is specified at TOUT register.
BitField.name: RTOIEN

BitField.description: Data Input Time-out Interrupt Enable Bit\nEnable/Disable interrupts generation of SD controller when data input time-out. Time-out value is specified at TOUT register.
BitField.name: DITOIEN

BitField.description: Wake-up Signal Generating Enable Bit\nEnable/Disable wake-up signal generating of SD controller when card is inserted or removed.
BitField.name: WKIEN

BitField.description: SD Card Detect Source Selection
BitField.name: CDSRC

BitField.description: Block Transfer Done Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates that SD host has finished all data-in or data-out block transfer. If there is a CRC16 error or incorrect CRC status during multiple block data transfer, the transfer will be broken and this bit will also be set.\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: BLKDIF

BitField.description: CRC7, CRC16 and CRC Status Error Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates that SD host has occurred CRC error during response in, data-in or data-out (CRC status error) transfer. When CRC error is occurred, software should reset SD engine. Some response (ex. R3) doesn't have CRC7 information with it; SD host will still calculate CRC7, get CRC error and set this flag. In this condition, software should ignore CRC error and clears this bit manually.\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: CRCIF

BitField.description: CRC7 Check Status (Read Only)\nSD host will check CRC7 correctness during each response in. If that response does not contain CRC7 information (ex. R3), then software should turn off CRCIEN (SDH_INTEN[1]) and ignore this bit.
BitField.name: CRC7

BitField.description: CRC16 Check Status of Data-in Transfer (Read Only)\nSD host will check CRC16 correctness after data-in transfer.
BitField.name: CRC16

BitField.description: CRC Status Value of Data-out Transfer (Read Only)\nSD host will record CRC status of data-out transfer. Software could use this value to identify what type of error is during data-out transfer.
BitField.name: CRCSTS

BitField.description: DAT0 Pin Status of Current Selected SD Port (Read Only)\nThis bit is the DAT0 pin status of current selected SD port.
BitField.name: DAT0STS

BitField.description: SD Card Detection Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates that SD card is inserted or removed. Only when CDIEN (SDH_INTEN[8]) is set to 1, this bit is active.\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: CDIF

BitField.description: Response Time-out Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates that SD host counts to time-out value when receiving response or R2 (waiting start bit).\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: RTOIF

BitField.description: Data Input Time-out Interrupt Flag (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates that SD host counts to time-out value when receiving data (waiting start bit).\nNote: This bit is read only, but can be cleared by writing '1' to it.
BitField.name: DITOIF

BitField.description: Card Detect Status of SD (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the card detect pin status of SD, and is used for card detection. When there is a card inserted in or removed from SD, software should check this bit to confirm if there is really a card insertion or removal.
BitField.name: CDSTS

BitField.description: DAT1 Pin Status of SD Card (Read Only)\nThis bit indicates the DAT1 pin status of SD card.
BitField.name: DAT1STS

BitField.description: SD Receiving Response Token 0\nSD host controller will receive a response token for getting a reply from SD card when RIEN (SDH_CTL[1]) is set. This field contains response bit 47-16 of the response token.
BitField.name: RESPTK0

BitField.description: SD Receiving Response Token 1\nThe SD host controller will receive a response token for getting a reply from SD card when RIEN (SDH_CTL[1]) is set. This register contains the bit 15-8 of the response token.
BitField.name: RESPTK1

BitField.description: SD BLOCK LENGTH in Byte Unit\nAn 11-bit value specifies the SD transfer byte count of a block. The actual byte count is equal to BLKLEN+1.\nNote: The default SD block length is 512 bytes
BitField.name: BLKLEN

BitField.description: SD Response/Data-in Time-out Value\nA 24-bit value specifies the time-out counts of response and data input. SD host controller will wait start bit of response or data-in until this value reached. The time period depends on SD engine clock frequency. Do not write a small number into this field, or you may never get response or data due to time-out.\nNote: Filling 0x0 into this field will disable hardware time-out function.
BitField.name: TOUT

BitField.description: SDH Shared Buffer\nSingle 128 Bytes shared buffer for data exchange between system memory and cards.
BitField.name: SB

BitField.description: SD BLOCK LENGTH in Byte Unit\nAn 11-bit value specifies the SD transfer byte count of a block. The actual byte count is equal to BLKLEN+1.\nNote: The default SD block length is 512 bytes
BitField.name: BLKLEN

BitField.description: SD Response/Data-in Time-out Value\nA 24-bit value specifies the time-out counts of response and data input. SD host controller will wait start bit of response or data-in until this value reached. The time period depends on SD engine clock frequency. Do not write a small number into this field, or you may never get response or data due to time-out.\nNote: Filling 0x0 into this field will disable hardware time-out function.
BitField.name: TOUT

BitField.description: Slot Controller 1 Done Interrupt Enable Bit\nThis field is used to enable Slot controller 1 finish interrupt.

BitField.description: Configurable Interrupt 0 Flag \nThe setting interrupt is trigger at the end of the check point of the pin.\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: CON0IF

BitField.description: Configurable Interrupt 1 Flag \nThe setting interrupt is trigger at the end of the check point of the pin.\nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: CON1IF

BitField.description:
Mismatch Interrupt Flag
This flag shows the amounts of data are not the same in each pins with PDMA enabled. If this situation happens, all slot controllers stop counting.
Note 1: This flag is only effective on the pin with PDMA enabled.
Note 2: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: MISMATIF

BitField.description:
Transfer Error Interrupt Status Flag 
This field is used for transfer error interrupt status flag. The transfer error states is at PSIO_TRANSTS register which includes input data overflow flag INOVERn (PSIO_TRANSTS[29,25,21,17,13,9,5,1] and output data underflow flag OUTUFn (PSIO_TRANSTS[31,27,23,19,15,11,7,3]).
Note 1: This field is the status flag of INOVER or OUTUFER.
Note 2: This bit can only be cleared by writing 1 to coordinate transfer error.
BitField.name: TERRIF

BitField.description: Slot Controller 0 Counting Done Interrupt Status Flag\nThis field is used for slot controller 0 finish interrupt status flag. \nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: SC0IF

BitField.description: Slot Controller 1 Counting Done Interrupt Status Flag\nThis field is used for slot controller 1 finish interrupt status flag. \nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: SC1IF

BitField.description: Slot Controller 2 Counting Done Interrupt Status Flag\nThis field is used for slot controller 2 finish interrupt status flag. \nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: SC2IF

BitField.description: Slot Controller 3 Counting Done Interrupt Status Flag\nThis field is used for slot controller 3 finish interrupt status flag. \nNote: This bit can be cleared by writing 1.
BitField.name: SC3IF

BitField.description: Input Data Full Flag0 (Read Only)\nNote: This bit will be cleared automatically when related slot controller started and pin enabled.
BitField.name: INFULL0

BitField.description:
Input Data Overflow Flag0
Note 1: When input Overflow happened, it will keep the current data, and discard the upcoming data.
Note 2: When overflow happens, related slot controller will be stopped.
Note 3: This bit can be cleared by configure 1 to it.
Note 4: This bit will be cleared automatically when related slot controller started and pin enabled.
BitField.name: INOVER0

BitField.description: Output Data Empty Flag0 (Read Only)
BitField.name: OUTEPY0

BitField.description:
Output Data Underflow Flag0
When PSIO is still output data but PSIOn_OUTDAT have not been ready. This flag will be set to 1.
Note 1: When output data shortage happened, it will output 0.
Note 2: When underflow happens, related slot controller will be stopped.
Note 3: This bit can be cleared by configure 1 to it.
Note 4: This bit will be cleared automatically when related slot controller started and pin enabled.
